# Solana Developer Platform

> Full public documentation for Solana Developer Platform — all page content for AI and agent ingestion.

## Canonical URLs
- Docs: https://platform.solana.com/docs
- API: https://api.solana.com
- Interactive API docs: https://api.solana.com/docs
- OpenAPI: https://api.solana.com/openapi.json
- AI guide: https://platform.solana.com/docs/reference/docs-for-ai

## Docs

### What is SDP?
Source: https://platform.solana.com/docs/introduction

> One API for tokenization, custody, payments, and compliance on Solana.

SDP gives you tokenization, custody, payments, and compliance through one API. The API stays the same
when you change providers. Every operation authenticates against a project.

| Module | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| **Issuance** | Deploy, mint, burn, freeze, pause, and seize tokens built on Token-2022 |
| **Custody** | Provision and operate Solana wallets through interchangeable custody providers |
| **Payments** | Move funds onchain: transfers, batches, recurring payments, payment requests, and ramps |
| **Compliance** | Screen wallets and transactions against your regulatory program |

## Background

Institutional capital is moving onchain. Public blockchains now hold
[$35 billion in tokenized real-world assets](https://app.rwa.xyz/), and
[$3.2 billion of that sits on Solana](https://app.rwa.xyz/networks/solana).
[Tokenized stocks](https://app.rwa.xyz/stocks) grow fastest, and Solana settles most of their
trading volume.

Assets at this scale need regulated custody, enforceable compliance, and auditable controls. SDP
gives you all three through one API. You do not need a team of Solana developers to bring an asset
onchain.

## Core features

<Steps>
<Step>
### One interface for every provider

SDP puts one API in front of the providers in the Solana ecosystem. You integrate once. You can
then add a provider, or change to another one, without changing your code.

The onramp call below works for every ramp provider. Only the `provider` field changes.

<Tabs items={["JavaScript", "Python", "curl"]}>
<Tab value="JavaScript">
```javascript title="onramp-quote.js" rotate-providers
const response = await fetch(
  "https://api.solana.com/v1/payments/ramps/onramp/quote",
  {
    method: "POST",
    headers: {
      Authorization: "Bearer sk_test_...",
      "Content-Type": "application/json",
    },
    body: JSON.stringify({
      provider: "moonpay",
      counterpartyId: "cp_...",
      destinationCustodyWalletId: "cwlt_...",
      assetRail: "usdc.solana",
      fiatCurrency: "USD",
      fiatAmount: "100.00",
    }),
  },
);
const quote = await response.json();
```
</Tab>
<Tab value="Python">
```python title="onramp_quote.py" rotate-providers

response = requests.post(
    "https://api.solana.com/v1/payments/ramps/onramp/quote",
    headers={"Authorization": "Bearer sk_test_..."},
    json={
        "provider": "moonpay",
        "counterpartyId": "cp_...",
        "destinationCustodyWalletId": "cwlt_...",
        "assetRail": "usdc.solana",
        "fiatCurrency": "USD",
        "fiatAmount": "100.00",
    },
)
quote = response.json()
```
</Tab>
<Tab value="curl">
```bash title="Terminal" rotate-providers
curl -X POST https://api.solana.com/v1/payments/ramps/onramp/quote \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer sk_test_..." \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "provider": "moonpay",
    "counterpartyId": "cp_...",
    "destinationCustodyWalletId": "cwlt_...",
    "assetRail": "usdc.solana",
    "fiatCurrency": "USD",
    "fiatAmount": "100.00"
  }'
```
</Tab>
</Tabs>
</Step>
<Step>
### Wallet custody

Create signing wallets through a custody provider. Your team never handles a private key.

A hosted key never leaves the provider's MPC or TEE infrastructure. SDP receives only the signed
transaction. SDP encrypts local development keys at rest with `AES-256-GCM`, using a key derived
per organization. Every signing request passes a policy check and a permission check before it
runs.

- **Built on `@solana/keychain`**

   `@solana/keychain` is the common signing interface for Solana. Each custody provider is an
   adapter behind that interface. This is what lets you change providers.

- **[Wallet policies](/docs/wallet-operations/policies)**

   A policy limits how a wallet moves funds. It can restrict destinations, cap amounts, allow or
   deny operations, and require an approval. SDP applies the policy before the operation runs.

- **Custody settings resolve by scope**

   SDP reads custody settings from the project first, then the organization, then the environment.
   Two teams can therefore run two different providers side by side.
</Step>
<Step>
### Issuance and compliance with Token-2022

Create a token from a template, such as a stablecoin or a tokenized security. You can also
configure your own token with Token-2022 extensions. Deploy the token, then mint, burn, and manage
its supply from the dashboard or the API.

The same extensions make compliance enforceable onchain. You can freeze one balance, pause all
transfers, seize tokens, and manage the token's **Token Access Control** list. Some compliance
actions accept a reason or a memo for the audit trail. Each action is one POST to the same token
endpoints.

<Tabs items={["JavaScript", "Python", "curl"]}>
<Tab value="JavaScript">
```javascript title="compliance-action.js" rotate-token-ops
const response = await fetch(
  "https://api.solana.com/v1/issuance/tokens/tok_abc123/freeze",
  {
    method: "POST",
    headers: {
      Authorization: "Bearer sk_test_...",
      "Content-Type": "application/json",
    },
    body: JSON.stringify(operationParams),
  },
);
const result = await response.json();
```
</Tab>
<Tab value="Python">
```python title="compliance_action.py" rotate-token-ops

response = requests.post(
    "https://api.solana.com/v1/issuance/tokens/tok_abc123/freeze",
    headers={"Authorization": "Bearer sk_test_..."},
    json=operation_params,
)
result = response.json()
```
</Tab>
<Tab value="curl">
```bash title="Terminal" rotate-token-ops
curl -X POST https://api.solana.com/v1/issuance/tokens/tok_abc123/freeze \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer sk_test_..." \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d "$OPERATION_PARAMS"
```
</Tab>
</Tabs>
</Step>
<Step>
### Ramps and onchain transfers

SDP gives you one set of endpoints for onchain transfers and for ramps, across every provider. They
build on the official Solana programs
[Subscriptions](https://github.com/solana-program/subscriptions) and
[Solana Pay](https://github.com/solana-foundation/pay). SDP uses these programs for recurring
payments, payment requests, and batch transfers.

<Tabs items={["Recurring Payments", "Payment Requests", "Batch Transfers"]}>
<Tab value="Recurring Payments">
```bash title="Terminal"
curl -X POST https://api.solana.com/v1/payments/recurring-payments \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer sk_test_..." \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "sourceCustodyWalletId": "cwlt_123",
    "counterpartyId": "cp_...",
    "counterpartyAccountId": "cpa_...",
    "token": "USDC",
    "amount": "25.00",
    "periodHours": 720
  }'
```
</Tab>
<Tab value="Payment Requests">
```bash title="Terminal"
curl -X POST https://api.solana.com/v1/payments/requests \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer sk_test_..." \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "walletId": "privy_wallet_123",
    "counterpartyId": "cp_...",
    "token": "USDC",
    "amount": "25.00",
    "expiresAt": "2027-08-31T00:00:00.000Z"
  }'
```
</Tab>
<Tab value="Batch Transfers">
```bash title="Terminal"
curl -X POST https://api.solana.com/v1/payments/transfer-batches \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer sk_test_..." \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "externalId": "payroll_2026_06_30",
    "sourceCustodyWalletId": "cwlt_example",
    "token": "USDC",
    "recipients": [
      {
        "externalId": "payroll_row_001",
        "counterpartyId": "cp_...",
        "counterpartyAccountId": "cpa_...",
        "amount": "25.00"
      }
    ]
  }'
```
</Tab>
</Tabs>

The same API covers onramps and offramps. Rate estimates, quotes, and settlement behave the same way
for every provider and every corridor.

Money can therefore enter as fiat, stay onchain as a token you issued, and leave again as fiat. You
get the full cycle, from issuance to circulation to redemption, without a separate integration for
each provider.

See [Payments](/docs/payments) for transfers. See [Ramps](/docs/payments/ramps) for the supported
providers, currencies, and corridors.
</Step>
<Step>
### Audit trails

SDP records every sensitive operation. You can query the records for your organization.

Each entry holds the user or API key that acted, the resource it touched, and whether the operation
succeeded. It also holds the client IP address, the user agent, the request ID, and metadata with
the secrets removed.

| Area                    | Recorded events                                                                    |
| ----------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| API keys                | Create, revoke, and rotate, for both organization and project-scoped keys          |
| Token issuance          | Deploy, mint, burn, force-burn, supply changes, and authority updates              |
| Compliance actions      | Freeze, unfreeze, pause, unpause, seize, and Token Access Control changes          |
| Custody                 | Provider configuration, wallet provisioning, and credential lifecycle changes      |
| Transactions & signing  | Signing requests, submissions, and failed submissions                              |
| Organization & access   | Members, invitations, projects, project membership, and login sessions             |
| Counterparties & assets | Counterparty and Counterparty Account changes, asset profile changes               |
</Step>
</Steps>

---

## Developing with SDP

### Overview
Source: https://platform.solana.com/docs/developing-with-sdp

> Learn the two SDP interfaces, the two environments, and the response format every route uses.

SDP gives you two interfaces: the dashboard and the REST API. Both run against the same backend,
and both enforce the same permissions, policies, and audit records.

- **The dashboard** is a browser application for setup, token management, and compliance
  operations. Sign in with an email address, a Google account, or a GitHub account.
- **The REST API** is for backend integrations. Every route reads an API key from the
  `Authorization` header.

The API covers everything the dashboard does. Build against the API for automation and
integrations. Use the dashboard to set up your organization, inspect state, and run a single
operation by hand.

## Environments

The environment belongs to the **project**, not to an individual request. Every tenant resource and
every API key belongs to a project, and takes that project's environment.

| Environment  | Solana cluster | API key prefix |
| ------------ | -------------- | -------------- |
| `sandbox`    | devnet         | `sk_test_`     |
| `production` | mainnet        | `sk_live_`     |

Both environments have the same routes. Develop and test your integration against a sandbox
project. To move to production, change the API key.

## Response conventions

Every successful response wraps its payload in a `data` envelope, next to the metadata of the
request:

```json
{
  "data": { ... },
  "meta": { "requestId": "req_...", "timestamp": "2027-07-31T12:00:00.000Z" }
}
```

An error returns a `code` for your code to read, and a `message` for a person to read:

```json
{
  "error": { "code": "INVALID_API_KEY", "message": "Invalid API key" }
}
```

Include the `requestId` when you report a problem. It links your request to the internal traces and
audit records.

## Execution model

SDP runs a custody operation in three steps. SDP builds the transaction, signs it with the
configured custody wallet, and submits it.

---

### Idempotency
Source: https://platform.solana.com/docs/developing-with-sdp/idempotency

> Replay a mutation safely with the Idempotency-Key header, which the created record claims.

Retries are part of every distributed system. A client times out, a connection drops, or a worker
stops in the middle of a run.

SDP lets you replay a mutation safely. Send an `Idempotency-Key` header with a unique value. A UUID
works well. Create that value once per logical operation, and send the same value on every retry of
that operation.

```bash title="Terminal"
curl -X POST https://api.solana.com/v1/payments/transfers \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer sk_test_..." \
  -H "Idempotency-Key: 8a2f6c1e-9d4b-4f3a-b7e5-2c8d9f0a1b3c" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{ ... }'
```

## How replay resolution works

The SDP model is not a response cache. The **business record** claims the idempotency key, not a
snapshot of the first response.

1. The first request creates the record. The record is a transfer, a batch, or an issuance
   transaction. It carries your key and a fingerprint of the normalized request payload.
2. A retry with the same key and the same payload returns **HTTP 200 with the stored record**, in
   the normal success envelope. The response is the live record, not a cached copy, so a replay
   shows the current state. A transfer that has finalized since the first attempt comes back as
   `finalized`, not as the `processing` you saw first.
3. A request with the same key and a **different payload** returns **409 `CONFLICT`**, with the
   message "Idempotency key already used with different request payload". SDP normalizes each field
   before it compares the fingerprints, so a difference in formatting does not create a false
   conflict.

SDP keeps a key for as long as the record that claimed it exists. There is no time to live, and a
replay works for as long as the record exists.

SDP validates the header on every `/v1` route. The value must be 1 to 255 printable ASCII
characters. Only the endpoints below act on it. Every other route accepts the header and ignores
it.

## Where it applies

Each domain claims a key in its own namespace, and the namespaces have different scopes:

| Domain | Operations | Key namespace |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Payments (transfers) | `POST /v1/payments/transfers` | Per project |
| Payments (batches) | `POST /v1/payments/transfer-batches` | Per project |
| Issuance | Execute-mode deploy, mint, burn, force-burn, freeze, thaw, pause, unpause, seize, and authority transfer | Per organization, shared across **all** issuance operations and tokens |
| Custody | Provider credential submission (dashboard flow) | Required on every submission |

The namespaces are independent across domains. The same key value on a transfer and on a mint makes
two separate claims, and they never collide.

Inside issuance the namespace covers the whole organization. If you reuse a key for a different
issuance operation, SDP returns 409, even when the operation targets a different token.

## This model is open to change

The differences between domains above follow the order in which these API areas shipped. They are
not a finished design, and we expect them to converge.

Treat the core contract as stable: one key per logical operation, a replay returns the record, and
a payload mismatch returns 409.

Treat the scoping details as open to change: which namespace is per project versus per
organization, and which endpoints act on the header. We are considering two changes. We may act on
the header on more mutation endpoints, and we may give every domain the same namespace scope.

---

### Authentication
Source: https://platform.solana.com/docs/developing-with-sdp/authentication

> Authenticate an API request with a project-scoped API key, and see the controls that key carries.

SDP authenticates an API request with an API key that belongs to one project. Several controls
apply to the same key: its role, its per-key permissions, its wallet bindings, its policy profiles,
and its IP allowlist. Together they limit the key to the access its integration needs, and no more.

An authenticated API request carries the API key in the `Authorization` header:

```bash title="Terminal"
curl https://api.solana.com/v1/wallets \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer sk_test_..."
```

The `Bearer` prefix is optional. SDP also accepts a raw key in the `Authorization` header.

## Key scope

SDP issues a key for one **project**, and the key takes that project's environment. A `sk_test_`
key belongs to a sandbox project, which runs on devnet. A `sk_live_` key belongs to a production
project, which runs on mainnet.

A key reaches only the wallets, tokens, and payments of the project it was issued for. There is no
key that covers several projects, and no key that covers a whole organization.

## Authorization layers

A request must pass every layer that its key has configured:

| Layer | What it controls |
| --- | --- |
| **Role** | The baseline set of permissions. See the role table below. |
| **Per-key permissions** | Optional overrides of the role's defaults, one permission at a time. A key can hold only the permissions its creator holds. |
| **Wallet bindings** | The custody wallets the key can operate. Each binding has its own permission list. |
| **Policy profiles** | Rule sets that SDP evaluates before a bound wallet moves funds. A rule can restrict a destination, cap an amount, or require an approval. |
| **IP allowlist** | Optional IPv4, IPv6, or CIDR ranges that the key can be used from. |

| Role | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `api_admin` | Full access, including custody operations and platform operations. |
| `api_developer` | Read and write access to tokens, payments, counterparties, wallets, and webhooks. It excludes custody administration. |
| `api_readonly` | Read-only access to every resource, including audit records. |

## Errors

Your code can tell every authentication failure and authorization failure apart:

| Condition | Status | Code |
| --- | --- | --- |
| The request needs a key and carries none | 401 | `UNAUTHORIZED` |
| The key is malformed or unknown | 401 | `INVALID_API_KEY` |
| You deleted the key, or SDP revoked it | 401 | `REVOKED_API_KEY` |
| The key is past its expiry date or its rotation deadline | 401 | `EXPIRED_API_KEY` |
| The request comes from an address outside the key's IP allowlist | 403 | `FORBIDDEN` |
| The key lacks a required permission | 403 | `INSUFFICIENT_PERMISSIONS` |
| The key is over its rate limit | 429 | `RATE_LIMITED` |

SDP rate limits each key separately. The standard tier allows 100 requests per minute.

See [Manage API keys](/docs/developing-with-sdp/manage-api-keys) to create, rotate, and delete a
key.

---

### Manage API keys
Source: https://platform.solana.com/docs/developing-with-sdp/manage-api-keys

> Create, rotate, and delete the API keys that authenticate your SDP API requests.

An API key authenticates an SDP API request. Each key belongs to a project, takes that project's
environment, and carries a role. A key can also carry finer controls. See
[Authentication](/docs/developing-with-sdp/authentication) for how SDP enforces each of those
layers.

SDP returns the full secret once, when you create the key and when you rotate it. SDP stores only a
salted hash and a display prefix. You cannot recover a lost key. You can only rotate it or replace
it.

Every key records `lastUsedAt`. Use that value to find a stale credential before you delete it.

## Key format

| Environment | Prefix | Solana cluster |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Sandbox | `sk_test_` | devnet |
| Production | `sk_live_` | mainnet |

## Roles

| Role | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `api_admin` | Full access, including custody operations and platform operations. |
| `api_developer` | Read and write access. It excludes custody actions. |
| `api_readonly` | Read-only access to every resource. |

A key can also carry explicit `permissions` that override the role's defaults. A key can hold only
the permissions its creator holds.

## Create a key

<Tabs items={["Dashboard", "API"]}>
<Tab value="Dashboard">

1. Select **API keys** in the sidebar. The list is empty until you create your first key.

   ![API keys page with no keys yet](/images/getting-started/api-keys-empty.png)

2. Select **New API key**.

3. Enter the key details:
   - **Name**. A descriptive label, for example "CI deploy key".
   - **Role**. **Admin**, **Developer**, or **Read only**.
   - **Wallet access**. **All wallets** or **Selected wallets**.
   - **Expiration (optional)**. A date and a time.

   ![Create API key modal](/images/getting-started/api-key-create.png)

4. Select **Continue**.

5. Review the summary, then select **Create key**.

   ![Review API key modal](/images/getting-started/api-key-review.png)

6. Select **Copy** on the **API key generated** dialog, and save the key. SDP does not show it
   again.

   ![API key generated modal showing the full key](/images/getting-started/api-key-generated.png)

7. Select **Dismiss**. The key now appears in the table with its prefix, role, environment, and
   status.

   ![API keys list with one active key](/images/getting-started/api-keys-list.png)

</Tab>
<Tab value="API">

<Tabs items={["curl", "TypeScript", "Java"]}>
<Tab value="curl">
```bash title="Terminal"
curl -X POST https://api.solana.com/v1/api-keys \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer sk_test_..." \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "name": "CI deploy key",
    "role": "api_developer",
    "walletScope": "all",
    "expiresAt": "2027-12-31T23:59:59Z"
  }'
```
</Tab>
<Tab value="TypeScript">
```typescript title="create-api-key.ts"
const response = await fetch("https://api.solana.com/v1/api-keys", {
  method: "POST",
  headers: {
    "Authorization": "Bearer sk_test_...",
    "Content-Type": "application/json",
  },
  body: JSON.stringify({
    name: "CI deploy key",
    role: "api_developer",
    walletScope: "all",
    expiresAt: "2027-12-31T23:59:59Z",
  }),
});
const { data } = await response.json();
// data.apiKey.key — save this, only shown once
```
</Tab>
<Tab value="Java">
```java title="CreateApiKey.java"
HttpRequest request = HttpRequest.newBuilder()
    .uri(URI.create("https://api.solana.com/v1/api-keys"))
    .header("Authorization", "Bearer sk_test_...")
    .header("Content-Type", "application/json")
    .POST(HttpRequest.BodyPublishers.ofString("""
        {
          "name": "CI deploy key",
          "role": "api_developer",
          "walletScope": "all",
          "expiresAt": "2027-12-31T23:59:59Z"
        }"""))
    .build();
```
</Tab>
</Tabs>

The new key belongs to the project of the key that created it, and takes that project's
environment. The request has no environment field.

The response includes the full `key` value. **Save it. SDP returns it only once.**

These fields are optional: `description`, `permissions` for finer overrides, `allowedIps` for IPv4,
IPv6, or CIDR ranges, `signingWalletId` and `signingWalletIds`, and `walletBindings` for per-wallet
permission lists.

</Tab>
</Tabs>

## Rotate a key

Rotation replaces the secret without a gap in availability. SDP creates a fresh key record that
copies the old key's role, permissions, IP allowlist, wallet bindings, and policy profiles. The old
key keeps working until its grace deadline.

Both keys are valid during the grace period. After the deadline, the old key fails with
`EXPIRED_API_KEY`.

<Tabs items={["Dashboard", "API"]}>
<Tab value="Dashboard">

1. Open the **Actions** menu next to the key in the API keys table.

2. Select **Rotate key (24h grace)**. The dashboard always uses a grace period of 24 hours. Use the
   API to set another value, from 0 to 168 hours.

   ![Actions dropdown showing Rotate key and Delete key options](/images/getting-started/api-key-rotate.png)

3. Copy the new key value from the **API key generated** dialog. SDP shows it once.

</Tab>
<Tab value="API">

<Tabs items={["curl", "TypeScript", "Java"]}>
<Tab value="curl">
```bash title="Terminal"
curl -X POST https://api.solana.com/v1/api-keys/key_abc123/rotate \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer sk_test_..." \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{ "gracePeriodHours": 24 }'
```
</Tab>
<Tab value="TypeScript">
```typescript title="rotate-api-key.ts"
const response = await fetch(
  "https://api.solana.com/v1/api-keys/key_abc123/rotate",
  {
    method: "POST",
    headers: {
      "Authorization": "Bearer sk_test_...",
      "Content-Type": "application/json",
    },
    body: JSON.stringify({ gracePeriodHours: 24 }),
  }
);
const { data } = await response.json();
// data.apiKey — the new key, only shown once
// data.previousKey.rotationDeadline — when the old key stops working
```
</Tab>
<Tab value="Java">
```java title="RotateApiKey.java"
HttpRequest request = HttpRequest.newBuilder()
    .uri(URI.create("https://api.solana.com/v1/api-keys/key_abc123/rotate"))
    .header("Authorization", "Bearer sk_test_...")
    .header("Content-Type", "application/json")
    .POST(HttpRequest.BodyPublishers.ofString("""
        { "gracePeriodHours": 24 }"""))
    .build();
```
</Tab>
</Tabs>

`gracePeriodHours` accepts a value from 0 to 168. The default is 24. A key cannot rotate itself.
Authenticate the rotation with another key, or with a dashboard session.

</Tab>
</Tabs>

## Delete a key

<Tabs items={["Dashboard", "API"]}>
<Tab value="Dashboard">

1. Open the **Actions** menu next to the key.

2. Select **Delete key**.

3. Enter the key's name to confirm, then select **Delete key**.

The key stops working at once, and you cannot restore it. The row stays in the table.

</Tab>
<Tab value="API">

<Tabs items={["curl", "TypeScript", "Java"]}>
<Tab value="curl">
```bash title="Terminal"
curl -X DELETE https://api.solana.com/v1/api-keys/key_abc123 \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer sk_test_..." \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{ "confirmation": "CI deploy key" }'
```
</Tab>
<Tab value="TypeScript">
```typescript title="revoke-api-key.ts"
await fetch("https://api.solana.com/v1/api-keys/key_abc123", {
  method: "DELETE",
  headers: {
    "Authorization": "Bearer sk_test_...",
    "Content-Type": "application/json",
  },
  body: JSON.stringify({ confirmation: "CI deploy key" }),
});
```
</Tab>
<Tab value="Java">
```java title="RevokeApiKey.java"
HttpRequest request = HttpRequest.newBuilder()
    .uri(URI.create("https://api.solana.com/v1/api-keys/key_abc123"))
    .header("Authorization", "Bearer sk_test_...")
    .header("Content-Type", "application/json")
    .method("DELETE", HttpRequest.BodyPublishers.ofString("""
        { "confirmation": "CI deploy key" }"""))
    .build();
```
</Tab>
</Tabs>

The `confirmation` field must match the key's **name**.

The deletion takes effect at once, and you cannot undo it. The call is idempotent, so a second call
on the same key also succeeds. As with rotation, a key cannot delete itself.

</Tab>
</Tabs>

---

## Getting started

### Set up your organization and projects
Source: https://platform.solana.com/docs/guides/setup-organization

> Create your SDP organization, and learn how a project scopes the work inside it.

Every SDP user works inside an **organization**. An organization is a team workspace that holds one
or more **projects**. Each project is a provisioned environment with its own API keys, wallets, and
members.

This guide creates your organization. It then explains how a project scopes your resources.

## 1. Sign up

Go to [platform.solana.com](https://platform.solana.com) and select **Dashboard**. On the sign-in
screen, select **Sign up** to create an account.

![SDP sign-in screen with a Sign up link](/images/getting-started/sign-in.png)

Enter your email address and a password to create the account.

![Create your account screen](/images/getting-started/create-account.png)

## 2. Create or select an organization

After you sign in, SDP asks you to set up your organization.

1. Upload a logo.
2. Enter your organization name.
3. Select **Continue**.

![Setup your organization screen, with the logo and name fields filled in](/images/getting-started/setup-organization.png)

If you already belong to an organization, the sidebar shows its name. Select the name to open the
list of your organizations. From that list you can change organization, or create another one.

<img src="/docs/images/getting-started/org-switcher.png" alt="The open organization list, showing the current organization and its projects" width="436" style={{ display: "block", maxWidth: "100%" }} />

## 3. Organize with projects

A **project** is a provisioned environment inside your organization. It is a sandbox project or a
production project. Each project has its own API keys, wallets, tokens, and members, so two teams
do not share the same wallets and tokens.

See the [Projects API reference](/docs/reference/api/projects) to manage projects from your own
code.

## 4. Next steps

- [Set up wallets](/docs/guides/setup-wallets) to sign transactions.
- [Create API keys](/docs/developing-with-sdp/manage-api-keys) for access from your own code.
- [Create your first token](/docs/tokens/create-a-token).

---

### Set up wallets
Source: https://platform.solana.com/docs/guides/setup-wallets

> Initialize a custody provider, then create the custody wallets that sign your transactions.

A **custody wallet** is a Solana keypair that a custody provider holds and signs with. SDP sends
each signing request to the provider that holds the wallet's key.

Initialize a provider first. Then create the wallets that deploy tokens, mint tokens, send
transfers, and run other onchain operations.

## Supported providers

Four providers are available to every organization. The others need access to be granted for your
organization before the provider appears. Ask your SDP contact to grant that access.

| Provider | Description | Availability |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Privy** | An embedded wallet infrastructure platform. | Available to every organization |
| **Fireblocks** | A digital asset infrastructure company. | Access granted per organization |
| **Coinbase CDP** | Embedded wallets for developers. | Available to every organization |
| **Para** | A wallet and authentication suite. | Available to every organization |
| **Turnkey** | A non-custodial wallet infrastructure platform. | Available to every organization |
| **DFNS** | Digital asset wallet infrastructure. | Access granted per organization |
| **Anchorage** | Regulated institutional crypto custody. | Access granted per organization |

<Tabs items={["Dashboard", "API"]}>
<Tab value="Dashboard">

### 1. Open the Wallets page

Select **Wallets** in the sidebar. If you have not set up your organization yet, complete the
[organization setup](/docs/guides/setup-organization) first.

### 2. Choose a custody provider

The Wallets page shows the providers your organization can use. Each one has a **New wallet**
button. Choose the provider that fits your setup.

![Wallets page showing one card per custody provider, each with a New wallet button](/images/getting-started/wallet-providers.png)

### 3. Create the wallet

1. Select **New wallet** on the provider you chose.
2. Enter a label for the wallet.
3. Select **Create wallet**.

<img src="/docs/images/getting-started/wallet-create-modal.png" alt="The new wallet dialog, with the label field filled in" width="696" style={{ display: "block", maxWidth: "100%" }} />

### 4. View your wallet

SDP creates the wallet, then shows its card on the Wallets page with the wallet's address, wallet
ID, and balance.

![Wallets page showing the card of the new wallet](/images/getting-started/wallet-created.png)

To create another wallet, select **Create wallet** and repeat step 3.

### 5. Provider capabilities

Each provider supports a different set of operations. The wallet card shows them as chips:

- **Issuance**. The wallet can deploy and mint tokens.
- **Transfers**. The wallet can sign payment transactions.
- **Compliance**. The wallet can sign freeze and unfreeze instructions.

</Tab>
<Tab value="API">

#### 1. Initialize the signing provider

<Tabs items={["curl", "TypeScript", "Java"]}>
<Tab value="curl">
```bash title="Terminal"
curl -X POST https://api.solana.com/v1/wallets/initialize \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer sk_test_..." \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "provider": "privy",
    "walletLabel": "Master wallet"
  }'
```
</Tab>
<Tab value="TypeScript">
```typescript title="initialize-wallet-provider.ts"
const response = await fetch("https://api.solana.com/v1/wallets/initialize", {
  method: "POST",
  headers: {
    "Authorization": "Bearer sk_test_...",
    "Content-Type": "application/json",
  },
  body: JSON.stringify({
    provider: "privy",
    walletLabel: "Master wallet",
  }),
});
const { data } = await response.json();
// data: { configId, publicKey, walletId }
```
</Tab>
<Tab value="Java">
```java title="InitializeWalletProvider.java"
HttpRequest request = HttpRequest.newBuilder()
    .uri(URI.create("https://api.solana.com/v1/wallets/initialize"))
    .header("Authorization", "Bearer sk_test_...")
    .header("Content-Type", "application/json")
    .POST(HttpRequest.BodyPublishers.ofString("""
        {
          "provider": "privy",
          "walletLabel": "Master wallet"
        }"""))
    .build();
```
</Tab>
</Tabs>

#### 2. Create additional wallets

<Tabs items={["curl", "TypeScript", "Java"]}>
<Tab value="curl">
```bash title="Terminal"
curl -X POST https://api.solana.com/v1/wallets \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer sk_test_..." \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "label": "Mint authority wallet",
    "purpose": "mint_authority",
    "setDefault": false
  }'
```
</Tab>
<Tab value="TypeScript">
```typescript title="create-wallet.ts"
const response = await fetch("https://api.solana.com/v1/wallets", {
  method: "POST",
  headers: {
    "Authorization": "Bearer sk_test_...",
    "Content-Type": "application/json",
  },
  body: JSON.stringify({
    label: "Mint authority wallet",
    purpose: "mint_authority",
    setDefault: false,
  }),
});
```
</Tab>
<Tab value="Java">
```java title="CreateWallet.java"
HttpRequest request = HttpRequest.newBuilder()
    .uri(URI.create("https://api.solana.com/v1/wallets"))
    .header("Authorization", "Bearer sk_test_...")
    .header("Content-Type", "application/json")
    .POST(HttpRequest.BodyPublishers.ofString("""
        {
          "label": "Mint authority wallet",
          "purpose": "mint_authority",
          "setDefault": false
        }"""))
    .build();
```
</Tab>
</Tabs>

The `purpose` field is optional metadata in the API. The create-wallet flow in the dashboard does
not offer a wallet purpose.

#### 3. List wallets

<Tabs items={["curl", "TypeScript", "Java"]}>
<Tab value="curl">
```bash title="Terminal"
curl "https://api.solana.com/v1/wallets?view=summary" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer sk_test_..."
```
</Tab>
<Tab value="TypeScript">
```typescript title="list-wallets.ts"
const response = await fetch("https://api.solana.com/v1/wallets?view=summary", {
  headers: { "Authorization": "Bearer sk_test_..." },
});
const { data } = await response.json();
// data.wallets includes walletId, publicKey, provider, label, purpose, and status
```
</Tab>
<Tab value="Java">
```java title="ListWallets.java"
HttpRequest request = HttpRequest.newBuilder()
    .uri(URI.create("https://api.solana.com/v1/wallets?view=summary"))
    .header("Authorization", "Bearer sk_test_...")
    .GET()
    .build();
```
</Tab>
</Tabs>

`GET /v1/wallets` returns two identifiers for each wallet. `walletId` is the provider wallet ID,
for example `privy_wallet_123`. `id` is the SDP wallet ID, for example `cwlt_abc123`.

Use the provider wallet ID (`walletId`) to set the default wallet, and to bind an API key to a
wallet. Use the SDP wallet ID (`id`) as `sourceCustodyWalletId` or `destinationCustodyWalletId` on
the payments and ramps endpoints. See
[Which wallet identifier to use](/docs/wallet-operations#which-wallet-identifier-to-use) for the
full table.

#### 4. Set a default wallet

`POST /v1/wallets/default-wallet` takes the provider wallet ID in its `walletId` field. It does not
accept the SDP wallet ID, and it does not accept the wallet address.

<Tabs items={["curl", "TypeScript", "Java"]}>
<Tab value="curl">
```bash title="Terminal"
curl -X POST https://api.solana.com/v1/wallets/default-wallet \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer sk_test_..." \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{ "walletId": "privy_wallet_123" }'
```
</Tab>
<Tab value="TypeScript">
```typescript title="set-default-wallet.ts"
await fetch("https://api.solana.com/v1/wallets/default-wallet", {
  method: "POST",
  headers: {
    "Authorization": "Bearer sk_test_...",
    "Content-Type": "application/json",
  },
  body: JSON.stringify({ walletId: "privy_wallet_123" }),
});
```
</Tab>
<Tab value="Java">
```java title="SetDefaultWallet.java"
HttpRequest request = HttpRequest.newBuilder()
    .uri(URI.create("https://api.solana.com/v1/wallets/default-wallet"))
    .header("Authorization", "Bearer sk_test_...")
    .header("Content-Type", "application/json")
    .POST(HttpRequest.BodyPublishers.ofString("""
        { "walletId": "privy_wallet_123" }"""))
    .build();
```
</Tab>
</Tabs>

</Tab>
</Tabs>
