## Tokens

### Tokenize an asset
Source: https://platform.solana.com/docs/tokens/tokenize-an-asset

> Choose a token model, then follow the guides that take that asset onchain.

Use this page to issue a stablecoin, a tokenized security, a loyalty token, or another asset
through the Solana Developer Platform. It takes you from the business decision to the first API
call.

## Choose a token model

Select the **Template** that matches the compliance and operational requirements of your asset.

| Asset model | Template | Typical controls |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Fiat-backed stablecoin | `stablecoin` | Mint authority, freeze authority, pausable, permanent delegate |
| Tokenized security or RWA | `tokenized-security` | Allowlist on by default, freeze authority, pausable, permanent delegate |
| Loyalty, rewards, or utility token | `custom` | Manually selected extensions |
| Non-standard asset | `custom` | Manually selected extensions |

These templates cover the common cases. `GET /v1/issuance/templates` returns every template that is
available to your project.

Custody wallets hold the authorities of your token by default. SDP can therefore deploy the token,
mint supply, and run compliance actions without an external signer.

## Implementation sequence

Each step links to its own guide. Each guide gives instructions for the dashboard and for the API.

1. [Set up your organization and projects](/docs/guides/setup-organization)
2. [Set up wallets](/docs/guides/setup-wallets)
3. [Manage API keys](/docs/developing-with-sdp/manage-api-keys)
4. [Create a token](/docs/tokens/create-a-token). SDP saves the token as a draft.
5. [Deploy a token](/docs/tokens/deploy-a-token). SDP creates the mint account onchain.
6. [Mint and burn](/docs/tokens/mint-and-burn). Change the supply of the deployed token.
7. [Basic payment](/docs/payments/send-basic-payment). Transfer tokens between wallets.
8. [Allowlists](/docs/tokens/allowlists). Token Access Control, on by default for
   `tokenized-security`.
9. [Freeze and compliance](/docs/tokens/freeze-and-compliance). Freeze one balance, pause all
   transfers, or seize tokens.
10. [Manage token settings](/docs/tokens/manage-token-settings). Rotate or clear a token authority.

## Core API endpoints

| Method | Endpoint | Purpose |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `GET` | `/v1/issuance/templates` | List available token templates |
| `POST` | `/v1/issuance/tokens` | Create a token draft |
| `POST` | `/v1/issuance/tokens/{tokenId}/deploy` | Deploy the draft to Solana |
| `POST` | `/v1/issuance/tokens/{tokenId}/mint` | Mint new supply |
| `POST` | `/v1/issuance/tokens/{tokenId}/burn` | Reduce supply |
| `POST` | `/v1/issuance/tokens/{tokenId}/allowlist` | Add a Token Access Control entry |
| `POST` | `/v1/issuance/tokens/{tokenId}/freeze` | Freeze the balance of one holder |
| `POST` | `/v1/issuance/tokens/{tokenId}/pause` | Pause every transfer of the token |
| `POST` | `/v1/payments/transfers` | Transfer tokens |

See the full schema in the [Issuance API reference](/docs/reference/api/issuance) and the
[Payments API reference](/docs/reference/api/payments).

## Operational constraints

- SDP saves a new token as a **draft**. Deploy the draft before you mint or transfer the token.
- A paused token blocks minting and transfers. Unpause the token to run those operations again.
- Freeze and unfreeze accept the wallet address of a holder. SDP derives the associated token
  account from that address.
- Every SDP operation needs the matching authority on a custody wallet. If someone rotated an
  authority outside SDP, rotate it back to a controlled wallet. Do this before you deploy, mint, or
  run a compliance action.

## For AI agents

If you drive SDP through an agent workflow, start from
[Documentation for AI](/docs/reference/docs-for-ai). That page links the machine-readable SDP
discovery files. It also keeps AI-facing guidance grounded in the supported public API area.

---

### Create a token
Source: https://platform.solana.com/docs/tokens/create-a-token

> Define a new token from a template or your own configuration, and save it as a draft.

Creating a token defines its metadata, its extensions, and its operational rules. SDP saves the
result as a **draft**. A draft is not onchain yet. See [Deploy a token](/docs/tokens/deploy-a-token)
for the step that writes the mint account to Solana.

![Issuance page with no tokens yet and a card that starts a new token](/images/tokens/token-list-empty.png)

## Templates

| Template | Decimals | Key extensions | Use case |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `stablecoin` | 6 | Permanent delegate, pausable | USD-backed tokens |
| `tokenized-security` | 8 | Permanent delegate, pausable, scaled UI amount, allowlist on by default | Regulated assets |
| `custom` | 9 | None — you choose | Full control |

These templates cover the common cases. `GET /v1/issuance/templates` returns every template that is
available to your project.

## How it works

<HowItWorks>

<Step number={1} title="Choose a template">

Select the **Template** that matches your asset model. A template pre-fills a set of extensions and
constraints. You can review them before you save the draft.

<StepPanel>
<Tabs items={["UI", "API"]} groupId="how-it-works">
<Tab value="UI">

The dashboard shows a card for each template:

- **Stablecoin**. USD-backed tokens with compliance controls.
- **Tokenized Security**. Regulated assets with the allowlist on by default.
- **Custom**. A Token-2022 setup that you configure yourself.

To open those cards and pick one:

1. Select **Issuance** in the sidebar.
2. Select **Add new token** on an empty Issuance page. Select **New** when the list already holds
   tokens.
3. Select a template.
4. Select **Continue**.

![Template cards for Stablecoin, Tokenized Security, and Custom, with one card selected](/images/tokens/token-create-templates.png)

</Tab>
<Tab value="API">

List the templates to see which fields each one pre-configures:

```bash title="Terminal"
curl https://api.solana.com/v1/issuance/templates \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer sk_test_..."
```

```typescript title="list-templates.ts"
const res = await fetch("https://api.solana.com/v1/issuance/templates", {
  headers: { Authorization: "Bearer sk_test_..." },
});
const { data } = await res.json();
// data[].id — use as the "template" value when creating
```

</Tab>
</Tabs>
</StepPanel>

</Step>

<Step number={2} title="Configure token identity">

Set the core metadata of the token. This is the name, the symbol, the decimal count, and a URI that
points to your token metadata JSON.

<StepPanel>
<Tabs items={["UI", "API"]} groupId="how-it-works">
<Tab value="UI">

1. Enter the **Metadata URI**. This is an HTTPS URL for the token metadata JSON.
2. Enter the **Token Name**, for example `Acme Dollar`.
3. Enter the **Symbol**. Use 1 to 10 characters, made of letters, numbers, or periods.
4. Enter the **Decimals**. The selected template sets the default value.
5. Select **Continue**.

![Identity form with the Metadata URI, Token Name, Symbol, and Decimals fields completed](/images/tokens/token-create-identity.png)

</Tab>
<Tab value="API">

Pass the identity fields in the `POST /v1/issuance/tokens` body:

```bash title="Terminal"
curl -X POST https://api.solana.com/v1/issuance/tokens \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer sk_test_..." \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "name": "Acme Dollar",
    "symbol": "ACME",
    "decimals": 6,
    "description": "USD-backed stablecoin",
    "template": "stablecoin"
  }'
```

</Tab>
</Tabs>
</StepPanel>

</Step>

<Step number={3} title="Set operational settings">

Choose the custody wallet that deploys the token. Configure Token Access Control and the supply
controls in the same place.

<StepPanel>
<Tabs items={["UI", "API"]} groupId="how-it-works">
<Tab value="UI">

1. Select the **Main Signer**. This is the custody wallet that SDP uses for the deployment.
2. Set the transfer control. **Allowlist** lets only approved destinations receive the token.
   **Blocklist** blocks the listed destinations instead.
3. Select **Create draft** to save the token.

The `tokenized-security` template turns the allowlist on by default. You can change that setting
while the token is a draft.

![Operational settings with the Main Signer chosen and the Allowlist and Blocklist transfer controls visible](/images/tokens/token-create-settings.png)

</Tab>
<Tab value="API">

Add the operational fields to the same body.

`signingCustodyWalletId` is the exact SDP wallet `id` that `GET /v1/wallets` returns, for example
`cwlt_abc123`. Do not pass the provider-specific `walletId`. Do not pass the public key of the
wallet. You can omit the field while you draft the token and supply it when you deploy.

```typescript title="create-token.ts"
const res = await fetch("https://api.solana.com/v1/issuance/tokens", {
  method: "POST",
  headers: {
    Authorization: "Bearer sk_test_...",
    "Content-Type": "application/json",
  },
  body: JSON.stringify({
    name: "Acme Dollar",
    symbol: "ACME",
    decimals: 6,
    description: "USD-backed stablecoin",
    template: "stablecoin",
    signingCustodyWalletId: "cwlt_abc123",
    requiresAllowlist: false,
    isMintable: true,
    isFreezable: true,
  }),
});
```

For a custom token, omit `template` or set it to `"custom"`. Then pass `overrides.extensions`:

```typescript title="create-custom-token.ts"
body: JSON.stringify({
  name: "Game Coin",
  symbol: "GAME",
  decimals: 0,
  template: "custom",
  signingCustodyWalletId: "cwlt_abc123",
  overrides: {
    extensions: {
      pausable: {},
      transferFee: { basisPoints: 50, maxFee: "1000" },
    },
  },
  isMintable: true,
  isFreezable: false,
}),
```

</Tab>
</Tabs>
</StepPanel>

</Step>

<Step number={4} title="Confirm the draft">

SDP saves the token with the status `pending`. SDP writes nothing to Solana at this point.

<StepPanel>
<Tabs items={["UI", "API"]} groupId="how-it-works">
<Tab value="UI">

A success message confirms that SDP saved the draft. The token then appears in the **Issuance**
list with a **Draft** badge.

![Issuance list with the new token and its Draft badge](/images/tokens/token-list-draft.png)

Open the token to see its detail page. The status reads **Not deployed**, and a **Deploy** control
takes you to the next step.

![Token detail page with the status Not deployed and the Deploy control available](/images/tokens/token-detail-pending.png)

</Tab>
<Tab value="API">

A successful response returns the new token object:

```typescript title="create-token.ts"
const { data } = await res.json();
// data.token.id     — save this; used in all subsequent calls
// data.token.status — "pending"
// data.token.signingCustodyWalletId — exact wallet selected for deployment
```

The token is not onchain yet. Pass `data.token.id` to
[Deploy a token](/docs/tokens/deploy-a-token).

</Tab>
</Tabs>
</StepPanel>

</Step>

</HowItWorks>

---

### Deploy a token
Source: https://platform.solana.com/docs/tokens/deploy-a-token

> Write a token draft to Solana and confirm the mint account it creates.

After you [create a token](/docs/tokens/create-a-token), deploy it onchain. The deployment creates
the mint account on Solana. The custody wallet you select signs that transaction.

## Prerequisites

- A token draft with the status `pending`
- The exact SDP wallet `id` that `GET /v1/wallets` returns, for example `cwlt_abc123`

## How it works

<HowItWorks>

<Step number={1} title="Open the deploy action">

Find the draft that you want to deploy. Deployment is irreversible. SDP creates the mint account
and its configured authorities onchain, and you cannot undo that.

<StepPanel>
<Tabs items={["UI", "API"]} groupId="how-it-works">
<Tab value="UI">

1. Open the **Issuance** list.
2. Select the token that carries a **Draft** badge.

The token detail page shows a **Deploy** control. The same control appears in the fund management
panel.

![Token detail page for a draft, showing the status Not deployed and the Deploy control](/images/tokens/token-detail-pending.png)

</Tab>
<Tab value="API">

You need the `tokenId` that SDP returned when you created the token. If you do not have it, list
your tokens:

```bash title="Terminal"
curl https://api.solana.com/v1/issuance/tokens \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer sk_test_..."
```

Note the token `id`, for example `tok_abc123`. Every deploy call and every later call needs it.

List your wallets as well. Use the `id` of the wallet record. Do not use the provider-specific
`walletId`. Do not use the public key.

```bash title="Terminal"
curl https://api.solana.com/v1/wallets \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer sk_test_..."
```

</Tab>
</Tabs>
</StepPanel>

</Step>

<Step number={2} title="Deploy the token">

SDP signs and submits the deploy transaction with the wallet in `signingCustodyWalletId`.

If you supply that field here, it replaces the execution wallet stored on the draft. If you omit
it, SDP uses the value stored on the draft. One of the two values is required.

An override changes the deployment signer and the historical attribution. It does not rewrite the
immutable authority values already captured in the configuration of the token.

<StepPanel>
<Tabs items={["UI", "API"]} groupId="how-it-works">
<Tab value="UI">

1. Select **Deploy**. A dialog shows the signer wallet that authorizes the transaction.
2. Check the wallet ID and the public key in that dialog.
3. Select **Deploy now**.
4. Select **Deploy now** again in the confirmation prompt. That prompt asks you to confirm the
   onchain submission.

![Deploy dialog listing the signer wallet ID and public key that will authorize the deployment](/images/tokens/token-deploy-modal.png)

![Confirmation prompt asking you to confirm the onchain deploy submission](/images/tokens/token-deploy-confirm.png)

SDP submits the transaction to Solana and polls for confirmation. The page updates when the
deployment completes.

</Tab>
<Tab value="API">

```bash title="Terminal"
curl -X POST https://api.solana.com/v1/issuance/tokens/tok_abc123/deploy \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer sk_test_..." \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -H "Idempotency-Key: deploy-acme-001" \
  -d '{"signingCustodyWalletId":"cwlt_abc123"}'
```

```typescript title="deploy-token.ts"
const res = await fetch(
  "https://api.solana.com/v1/issuance/tokens/tok_abc123/deploy",
  {
    method: "POST",
    headers: {
      Authorization: "Bearer sk_test_...",
      "Content-Type": "application/json",
      "Idempotency-Key": "deploy-acme-001",
    },
    body: JSON.stringify({ signingCustodyWalletId: "cwlt_abc123" }),
  }
);
const { data } = await res.json();
// data.token.mintAddress — the onchain mint address
```

Always pass an `Idempotency-Key`. A retry with the same key after a network error prevents a second
deployment.

</Tab>
</Tabs>
</StepPanel>

</Step>

<Step number={3} title="Confirm the deployment">

When the network confirms the transaction, the token is active. You can then mint it and transfer
it.

<StepPanel>
<Tabs items={["UI", "API"]} groupId="how-it-works">
<Tab value="UI">

The status badge changes from **Not deployed** to the onchain mint address. The detail page then
shows the Mint and Burn actions in the Operations tab. The Transactions table shows the confirmed
deploy transaction.

![Deployed token detail page with the mint address, the Operations tab, and a confirmed deploy transaction](/images/tokens/token-deployed.png)

</Tab>
<Tab value="API">

The deploy response includes the confirmed state:

```typescript title="deploy-token.ts"
// data.token.status      — "active"
// data.token.mintAddress — e.g., "AcMeXYZ..."
// data.token.signingCustodyWalletId — exact wallet used for deployment
```

After the deployment, `signingCustodyWalletId` records historical deployment attribution only.

Mint and administrative actions resolve their current onchain authority. A standard burn uses its
exact source wallet. No later action falls back to the deployment wallet.

Fetch the token at any time to verify its state:

```bash title="Terminal"
curl https://api.solana.com/v1/issuance/tokens/tok_abc123 \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer sk_test_..."
```

</Tab>
</Tabs>
</StepPanel>

</Step>

</HowItWorks>

---

### Mint and burn
Source: https://platform.solana.com/docs/tokens/mint-and-burn

> Change the supply of a deployed token by minting to an address or burning from an account.

After you [deploy a token](/docs/tokens/deploy-a-token), you can mint new tokens to any address.
You can also burn tokens from an account that you control. Force-burn removes tokens from any
holder account without the signature of that holder.

## Prerequisites

- A deployed token with the status `active`
- The `tokens:write` permission on the API key, or `tokens:admin` for force-burn
- For a standard burn, the exact SDP wallet `id` that `GET /v1/wallets` returns, for example
  `cwlt_abc123`

## How it works

<HowItWorks>

<Step number={1} title="Select the token and the action">

Open the token that you want to manage. Mint and burn both start from the token detail page.

<StepPanel>
<Tabs items={["UI", "API"]} groupId="how-it-works">
<Tab value="UI">

1. Open the **Issuance** list.
2. Select an active token.

The fund management panel shows the current supply. It offers two actions, **Mint** and **Burn**.

![Token Operations tab with the current supply and the Mint and Burn actions available](/images/tokens/token-deployed.png)

</Tab>
<Tab value="API">

All supply operations share this URL pattern:

```text title="Endpoints"
POST /v1/issuance/tokens/{tokenId}/mint
POST /v1/issuance/tokens/{tokenId}/burn
POST /v1/issuance/tokens/{tokenId}/force-burn
```

The `amount` field is a decimal string in display units. `"1"` means one token. `"1.5"` means one
and a half tokens. SDP converts the value to onchain base units with the `decimals` of the token.

`signingCustodyWalletId` always means the exact SDP wallet `id`. It is never a provider-specific
`walletId` and never a public key.

A standard burn requires the field, because that wallet owns the source and signs for it. Mint and
force-burn treat the field as optional. When you do supply it, the wallet must control the current
mint authority or the current permanent-delegate authority.

When you omit the field, SDP requires exactly one accessible wallet to match that live authority.
A later action never falls back to the deployment wallet of the token.

</Tab>
</Tabs>
</StepPanel>

</Step>

<Step number={2} title="Mint tokens">

Issue new tokens to a destination address. SDP derives the associated token account from that
address.

<StepPanel>
<Tabs items={["UI", "API"]} groupId="how-it-works">
<Tab value="UI">

1. Select **Mint**. A dialog shows the signer wallet and a destination picker.
2. Select the destination wallet, or enter the destination address.
3. Enter the amount in display units, for example `1.0`.
4. Enter a memo. This field is optional, and SDP records the memo onchain.
5. Select **Mint tokens**.
6. Select **Mint now** in the confirmation prompt to submit the transaction onchain.

![Mint dialog with the destination, amount, and memo completed](/images/tokens/mint-modal-filled.png)

![Confirmation prompt for the mint transaction](/images/tokens/mint-confirm.png)

The message "Mint transaction finalized." appears when the network confirms the transaction. The
mint then appears in the Transactions table with the status `confirmed`.

![Transactions table with a confirmed mint entry and the finalized message](/images/tokens/mint-confirmed.png)

</Tab>
<Tab value="API">

```bash title="Terminal"
curl -X POST https://api.solana.com/v1/issuance/tokens/tok_abc123/mint \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer sk_test_..." \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -H "Idempotency-Key: mint-001" \
  -d '{
    "signingCustodyWalletId": "cwlt_abc123",
    "mint": {
      "destination": "7xKXz...9fGh",
      "amount": "1000",
      "memo": "Initial distribution"
    }
  }'
```

```typescript title="mint-tokens.ts"
const res = await fetch(
  "https://api.solana.com/v1/issuance/tokens/tok_abc123/mint",
  {
    method: "POST",
    headers: {
      Authorization: "Bearer sk_test_...",
      "Content-Type": "application/json",
      "Idempotency-Key": "mint-001",
    },
    body: JSON.stringify({
      signingCustodyWalletId: "cwlt_abc123",
      mint: {
        destination: "7xKXz...9fGh",
        amount: "1000",
        memo: "Initial distribution",
      },
    }),
  }
);
```

Set the priority with `options.priorityFee`. It accepts `"none"`, `"low"`, `"medium"`, `"high"`, or
a micro-lamport value.

</Tab>
</Tabs>
</StepPanel>

</Step>

<Step number={3} title="Burn tokens">

A standard burn reduces the supply from an account that your wallet controls. Force-burn reduces
the supply from any holder account, without the signature of that holder.

<StepPanel>
<Tabs items={["UI", "API"]} groupId="how-it-works">
<Tab value="UI">

1. Select **Burn**. A dialog shows the signer wallet and an empty source field.
2. Select the wallet that holds the tokens you want to remove.
3. Enter the amount.
4. Enter a memo. This field is optional.
5. Select **Burn tokens**.
6. Select **Burn now** in the confirmation prompt to submit the transaction onchain.

![Burn dialog with the source field still empty](/images/tokens/burn-modal-empty.png)

![Burn dialog with the source wallet list open](/images/tokens/burn-modal-source.png)

![Burn dialog with the source, amount, and memo completed](/images/tokens/burn-modal-filled.png)

![Confirmation prompt for the burn transaction](/images/tokens/burn-confirm.png)

The message "Burn transaction finalized." appears when the network confirms the transaction. The
burn then appears in the Transactions table with the status `confirmed`.

![Transactions table with a confirmed burn entry and the finalized message](/images/tokens/burn-confirmed.png)

**Force burn** needs the `tokens:admin` permission. Run it from the Compliance tab, not from the
Operations tab. Force burn removes tokens from any holder account without the signature of that
holder.

</Tab>
<Tab value="API">

Burn from an account that you control:

```typescript title="burn-tokens.ts"
await fetch("https://api.solana.com/v1/issuance/tokens/tok_abc123/burn", {
  method: "POST",
  headers: {
    Authorization: "Bearer sk_test_...",
    "Content-Type": "application/json",
    "Idempotency-Key": "burn-001",
  },
  body: JSON.stringify({
    signingCustodyWalletId: "cwlt_abc123",
    burn: { source: "3xYZa...2aBc", amount: "250", memo: "Redemption" },
  }),
});
```

Force-burn from any holder. This call needs the `tokens:admin` permission:

```typescript title="force-burn-tokens.ts"
await fetch("https://api.solana.com/v1/issuance/tokens/tok_abc123/force-burn", {
  method: "POST",
  headers: {
    Authorization: "Bearer sk_test_...",
    "Content-Type": "application/json",
    "Idempotency-Key": "force-burn-001",
  },
  body: JSON.stringify({
    signingCustodyWalletId: "cwlt_abc123",
    forceBurn: { source: "3xYZa...2aBc", amount: "250", memo: "Compliance action" },
  }),
});
```

</Tab>
</Tabs>
</StepPanel>

</Step>

<Step number={4} title="Check the supply">

SDP caches the total supply of a token. Confirm that the cached total reflects your mint or burn.

<StepPanel>
<Tabs items={["UI", "API"]} groupId="how-it-works">
<Tab value="UI">

The dashboard refreshes the supply after a confirmed operation. The Transactions table lists every
completed operation, including the deploy, the mint, and the burn, each with the status
`confirmed`.

![Transactions table with confirmed burn, mint, and deploy entries](/images/tokens/operations-history.png)

Select **Refresh supply** if the displayed value still looks stale.

</Tab>
<Tab value="API">

Call the refresh endpoint to update the cached total after a mint or a burn:

```bash title="Terminal"
curl -X POST https://api.solana.com/v1/issuance/tokens/tok_abc123/supply/refresh \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer sk_test_..."
```

The call is safe to include in an automated workflow that runs after a mint.

</Tab>
</Tabs>
</StepPanel>

</Step>

</HowItWorks>

---

### Allowlists
Source: https://platform.solana.com/docs/tokens/allowlists

> Control which addresses can receive your token by keeping a list of approved recipients.

**Token Access Control** decides who may hold or receive your token. This page covers its
`allowlist` mode.

A token created with `requiresAllowlist: true` enforces a list of approved destination addresses.
That check runs on the issuance flows that respect the allowlist, such as minting and
administrative transfers. The `tokenized-security` template turns the mode on by default.

Token Access Control is not the same thing as two other lists in SDP. The transfer allowlist of a
wallet belongs to a wallet policy. The Platform Allowlist controls admission to deployment. Keep
each one separate.

## Prerequisites

- A token created with `requiresAllowlist` enabled
- The `tokens:write` permission on the API key

## How it works

<HowItWorks>

<Step number={1} title="Enable the allowlist">

You configure the allowlist when you create the token. Decide before you create it whether your
token needs one. You cannot change the setting after the token is deployed.

<StepPanel>
<Tabs items={["UI", "API"]} groupId="how-it-works">
<Tab value="UI">

1. Open the **Create token** flow.
2. Open the operational settings.
3. Turn **Allowlist** on.

The `tokenized-security` template turns the allowlist on by default. You can change that setting
while the token is still a draft.

After the token is deployed, the **Operations** tab of the token detail page shows **Approved
recipients**. That section holds an Address field and a Label field. The Control Lists panel next
to it tracks the entry count and the frozen account count.

![Operational settings during token creation, with the Allowlist transfer control turned on](/images/tokens/token-create-settings.png)

</Tab>
<Tab value="API">

Set `requiresAllowlist: true` when you create the token:

```typescript title="enable-allowlist.ts"
body: JSON.stringify({
  name: "Acme Security",
  symbol: "ACMES",
  decimals: 8,
  template: "tokenized-security",
  requiresAllowlist: true,
  isMintable: true,
  isFreezable: true,
}),
```

After the deployment, SDP enforces the allowlist on the issuance flows that respect it.

</Tab>
</Tabs>
</StepPanel>

</Step>

<Step number={2} title="Add an address">

Add a wallet address to the allowlist before you mint to it. Add it before you use it as the
destination of an administrative transfer.

<StepPanel>
<Tabs items={["UI", "API"]} groupId="how-it-works">
<Tab value="UI">

1. Open the token detail page.
2. Open the **Operations** tab.
3. Select **Approved recipients**.
4. Enter the wallet address.
5. Enter a label. This field is optional.
6. Select **Approve recipient**.

SDP enforces the address on the next operation that checks the allowlist.

For an onchain list, SDP uses its authority wallet when exactly one custody wallet matches. If
several custody records match, select the signer in the confirmation dialog. A database-only list
needs no signer.

![Approved recipients section with empty Address and Label fields, ready for a new entry](/images/tokens/allowlist-empty.png)

The new entry then appears below the form, with a **Remove entry** control.

![Approved recipients list containing the new entry and its Remove entry control](/images/tokens/allowlist-entry-added.png)

</Tab>
<Tab value="API">

```bash title="Terminal"
curl -X POST https://api.solana.com/v1/issuance/tokens/tok_abc123/allowlist \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer sk_test_..." \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "address": "7xKXz...9fGh",
    "label": "Treasury wallet"
  }'
```

```typescript title="add-allowlist-entry.ts"
const res = await fetch(
  "https://api.solana.com/v1/issuance/tokens/tok_abc123/allowlist",
  {
    method: "POST",
    headers: {
      Authorization: "Bearer sk_test_...",
      "Content-Type": "application/json",
    },
    body: JSON.stringify({ address: "7xKXz...9fGh", label: "Treasury wallet" }),
  }
);
// res.data.entry.id — save this to remove the entry later
```

For an onchain addition, the JSON body accepts an optional `signingCustodyWalletId`. That value is
an exact `cwlt_…` record ID.

The wallet must control the current authority of the list. That authority can differ from the
freeze authority of the token. Without the selector, several matching custody records return
`409`. Selecting a wallet does not bypass the permission checks or the runtime availability
checks.

</Tab>
</Tabs>
</StepPanel>

</Step>

<Step number={3} title="Review the list">

Check which addresses are approved. Review the list before you mint to a new destination, and
during a compliance audit.

<StepPanel>
<Tabs items={["UI", "API"]} groupId="how-it-works">
<Tab value="UI">

The **Approved recipients** section shows every approved address, its label, and the date SDP
added it.

Use the search field to find an address by label or by public key.

</Tab>
<Tab value="API">

```bash title="Terminal"
curl "https://api.solana.com/v1/issuance/tokens/tok_abc123/allowlist?search=So1&label=Treasury" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer sk_test_..."
```

```typescript title="list-allowlist.ts"
const { data, meta } = await res.json();
// meta: { total, page, pageSize, hasMore }
```

Query parameters:

- `page`, `pageSize` — pagination (`pageSize` max 500, default 50).
- `search` — contains-style match over the entry address **and** label. A blank value is treated as no filter.
- `label` — restrict to entries with this exact label.

The search and the label filter both run on the server, across the whole list. The results are
therefore not limited to the current page.

To populate a label filter, fetch the distinct labels in use. The response also returns `total`,
the unfiltered entry count, for a summary display.

```bash
curl https://api.solana.com/v1/issuance/tokens/tok_abc123/allowlist/labels \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer sk_test_..."
```

```typescript
const { data } = await res.json();
// data: { labels: ["Market maker", "Treasury"], total: 42 }
```

</Tab>
</Tabs>
</StepPanel>

</Step>

<Step number={4} title="Remove an address">

Remove an address when the compliance status of a holder changes. Removal does not affect the
tokens that the holder already owns. It blocks only the future flows that enforce the allowlist.

<StepPanel>
<Tabs items={["UI", "API"]} groupId="how-it-works">
<Tab value="UI">

1. Open the **Operations** tab of the token detail page.
2. Select **Approved recipients**.
3. Select **Remove entry** next to the address.
4. Choose the signer in the confirmation dialog. This step applies to an onchain list when several
   custody wallets match.

The list and its count refresh after a successful removal.

</Tab>
<Tab value="API">

```bash title="Terminal"
curl -X DELETE \
  https://api.solana.com/v1/issuance/tokens/tok_abc123/allowlist/alw_abc123 \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer sk_test_..."
```

Use the `entry.id` that SDP returned when you added the address.

For an onchain removal, pass the optional exact signer as a query parameter:
`?signingCustodyWalletId=cwlt_example`.

To find the current authority of the list, request
`GET /v1/issuance/tokens/{tokenId}?includeAllowlistAuthority=true` and read
`data.allowlistAuthority`. That field is `null` for a database-only list.

Match that address against your wallets. Do not infer it from the freeze authority of the token.

</Tab>
</Tabs>
</StepPanel>

</Step>

</HowItWorks>

## Typical workflow for a tokenized security

1. Create the token with `requiresAllowlist: true` and the template `tokenized-security`.
2. [Deploy the token](/docs/tokens/deploy-a-token).
3. Collect wallet addresses from investors who passed KYC.
4. Add each verified address to the allowlist.
5. [Mint tokens](/docs/tokens/mint-and-burn) to the allowlisted addresses.
6. Remove an address when the compliance status of its holder changes.

---

### Freeze and compliance
Source: https://platform.solana.com/docs/tokens/freeze-and-compliance

> Screen an address, freeze one balance, pause all transfers, or seize tokens from a holder.

SDP gives you two kinds of compliance tooling for an issued token.

- **Token controls.** These are three separate operations. A freeze stops one holder from moving
  their balance. A pause stops every transfer of the token. A seize moves tokens away from a
  holder. Token controls need `isFreezable` on the token, or the `pausable` extension, depending
  on the operation.
- **Address screening.** Check a wallet against your configured compliance providers. Screen a
  wallet before you approve it as a destination, and before you add it to the Token Access Control
  allowlist of a token.

No compliance provider is enabled by default. Screening returns results only after an
administrator configures at least one provider for your organization.

Every token-control action needs the `tokens:admin` permission on the API key.

## How it works

<HowItWorks>

<Step number={1} title="Screen an address">

Check a Solana address against your configured compliance providers. Screen the address before you
onboard a wallet, and before you approve it as a transfer destination.

<StepPanel>
<Tabs items={["UI", "API"]} groupId="how-it-works">
<Tab value="UI">

1. Open the Compliance section of the dashboard.
2. Select **Screen address**.
3. Enter the wallet address.
4. Select the intent, for example a transfer destination or a candidate for the Token Access
   Control allowlist.

The dashboard returns one result for each provider. Each result shows a risk level, a risk score,
and any flags.

</Tab>
<Tab value="API">

```bash title="Terminal"
curl -X POST https://api.solana.com/v1/compliance/address-screenings \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer sk_test_..." \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "address": "8dHEsGLp...hQWRGZ",
    "network": "solana",
    "intent": "transfer_destination"
  }'
```

```typescript title="screen-address.ts"
const { data } = await res.json();
// data.screening.providers[]
// → { provider, status, riskScore, riskLevel, message, evaluatedAt }
```

See the [Compliance API reference](/docs/reference/api/compliance) for the full schema.

</Tab>
</Tabs>
</StepPanel>

</Step>

<Step number={2} title="Freeze and unfreeze one balance">

A freeze stops one holder from sending or receiving this token. It targets one associated token
account. Other holders keep their normal access, and the token itself stays active.

<StepPanel>
<Tabs items={["UI", "API"]} groupId="how-it-works">
<Tab value="UI">

1. Open the **Compliance** tab of the token detail page.
2. Select **Freeze or unfreeze a balance**.
3. Enter the wallet address of the holder.
4. Enter a reason. This field is optional.
5. Select **Freeze balance**.
6. Select **Freeze now** in the confirmation prompt to submit the transaction onchain.

![Freeze form with the wallet address and reason fields still empty](/images/tokens/freeze-controls-empty.png)

![Freeze form with the holder wallet address and a reason entered](/images/tokens/freeze-controls-filled.png)

![Confirmation prompt for the freeze transaction](/images/tokens/freeze-confirm.png)

The message "Freeze transaction finalized." appears, and the Frozen Accounts count changes to 1.

![Compliance tab with the finalized freeze message and a Frozen Accounts count of 1](/images/tokens/freeze-confirmed.png)

To lift a freeze:

1. Find the account in the frozen list.
2. Select **Unfreeze balance**.
3. Select **Unfreeze now** in the confirmation prompt to submit the transaction onchain.

![Confirmation prompt for the unfreeze transaction](/images/tokens/unfreeze-confirm.png)

The message "Unfreeze transaction finalized." appears, and the Frozen Accounts count returns to 0.

![Compliance tab with the finalized unfreeze message and a Frozen Accounts count of 0](/images/tokens/unfreeze-confirmed.png)

</Tab>
<Tab value="API">

Freeze one balance:

```bash title="Terminal"
curl -X POST https://api.solana.com/v1/issuance/tokens/tok_abc123/freeze \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer sk_test_..." \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "accountAddress": "3xYZa...2aBc",
    "reason": "Suspicious activity investigation"
  }'
```

`accountAddress` accepts the wallet address of a holder or its token account. SDP derives the
associated token account when it needs to.

Unfreeze that balance:

```typescript title="unfreeze-account.ts"
await fetch("https://api.solana.com/v1/issuance/tokens/tok_abc123/unfreeze", {
  method: "POST",
  headers: { Authorization: "Bearer sk_test_...", "Content-Type": "application/json" },
  body: JSON.stringify({ accountAddress: "3xYZa...2aBc" }),
});
```

List the frozen accounts:

```bash title="Terminal"
curl https://api.solana.com/v1/issuance/tokens/tok_abc123/frozen \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer sk_test_..."
```

</Tab>
</Tabs>
</StepPanel>

</Step>

<Step number={3} title="Pause and resume all transfers">

A pause stops every transfer and every mint of this token, for every holder. It is not a freeze. A
freeze affects one balance, and a pause affects the whole token. The token needs the `pausable`
extension.

<StepPanel>
<Tabs items={["UI", "API"]} groupId="how-it-works">
<Tab value="UI">

1. Open the **Compliance** tab of the token detail page.
2. Select **Pause Controls**.
3. Select **Pause token**.
4. Select the signer, if several custody records control the same authority. The prompt uses the
   only matching authority wallet when there is one. The unpause control follows the same rules.
5. Confirm the onchain submission in the prompt.

![Pause Controls with the Pause token and Unpause token controls](/images/tokens/pause-controls.png)

![Confirmation prompt for the pause transaction](/images/tokens/pause-confirm.png)

The message "Pause transaction finalized." appears, and an orange **Token is paused** banner
appears across the page. SDP then blocks every supply operation and every transfer.

![Compliance tab with the Token is paused banner and the finalized pause message](/images/tokens/pause-confirmed.png)

To resume transfers, select **Unpause token** and confirm.

![Confirmation prompt for the unpause transaction](/images/tokens/unpause-confirm.png)

</Tab>
<Tab value="API">

```bash title="Terminal"
# Pause
curl -X POST https://api.solana.com/v1/issuance/tokens/tok_abc123/pause \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer sk_test_..." \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"signingCustodyWalletId":"cwlt_example"}'

# Unpause
curl -X POST https://api.solana.com/v1/issuance/tokens/tok_abc123/unpause \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer sk_test_..." \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"signingCustodyWalletId":"cwlt_example"}'
```

`signingCustodyWalletId` is optional when exactly one in-scope custody record matches the current
pause authority. Send `{}` to use that resolution.

Several matches without a selector return `409`. An explicit choice must control the live
authority, and it must pass the authorization checks and the runtime checks. Reusing an
idempotency key with a different wallet returns `409`.

While the token is paused, SDP rejects every transfer operation and every supply operation. They
work again after an unpause.

</Tab>
</Tabs>
</StepPanel>

</Step>

<Step number={4} title="Seize tokens from a holder">

A seize transfers tokens from a holder to a recovery address, without the signature of that
holder. It moves the tokens; it does not freeze them and it does not pause the token. Use it for
court orders and regulatory enforcement. The action needs `tokens:admin`.

<StepPanel>
<Tabs items={["UI", "API"]} groupId="how-it-works">
<Tab value="UI">

1. Open the **Compliance** tab of the token detail page.
2. Select **Force transfer**.
3. Enter the source address.
4. Enter the destination address.
5. Enter the amount.
6. Enter a memo. Record a memo for the audit trail.
7. Select **Transfer now** to submit the transaction onchain.

</Tab>
<Tab value="API">

```bash title="Terminal"
curl -X POST https://api.solana.com/v1/issuance/tokens/tok_abc123/seize \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer sk_test_..." \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -H "Idempotency-Key: seize-001" \
  -d '{
    "seize": {
      "source": "3xYZa...2aBc",
      "destination": "9aBCd...4eEf",
      "amount": "250",
      "memo": "Court order #12345"
    }
  }'
```

</Tab>
</Tabs>
</StepPanel>

</Step>

</HowItWorks>

## Compliance response workflow

1. Screen the address through the Compliance API.
2. Freeze the balance of the affected holder while you investigate.
3. Act on the findings. Unfreeze the balance if the holder is cleared. Seize the tokens to a
   recovery address if you must move them. Force-burn the tokens if you must remove them from
   circulation. See [Mint and burn](/docs/tokens/mint-and-burn).
4. Record every action in a `memo` field for the audit trail.

---

### Manage token settings
Source: https://platform.solana.com/docs/tokens/manage-token-settings

> Review a deployed token, then rotate or clear one of its authorities.

After you deploy a token, you can rotate its authorities and adjust its operational settings.

Authority management is not a compliance action. For freeze, pause, and seize, see
[Freeze and compliance](/docs/tokens/freeze-and-compliance).

## Choosing the signer for a metadata edit

`PATCH /v1/issuance/tokens/{tokenId}` accepts an optional `signingCustodyWalletId` for an onchain
metadata edit.

That field selects the exact custody record that controls the current metadata authority, for this
request only. It does not set a new deployment wallet, and it does not set a new authority.

If you omit the field, SDP requires exactly one matching in-scope record. Several matches return
`409`. A database-only edit needs no signer.

In the dashboard, SDP uses the one matching wallet automatically. When several wallets match,
choose one in the metadata confirmation, or beside the Save control for the asset profile. The
historical `data.token.signingCustodyWalletId` value does not change.

To find that signer after someone rotated the authority outside SDP, request
`GET /v1/issuance/tokens/{tokenId}?includeMetadataAuthority=true` and read `data.metadataAuthority`.

For a token that has a mint, SDP reads that value live from the chain. The stored snapshot in
`data.token.metadataAuthority` can therefore differ. A token without a mint returns its stored
metadata authority, or its mint authority, with no RPC call.

An RPC failure returns `502`. SDP never falls back to the stored value. The dashboard keeps
metadata errors and allowlist lookup errors separate, and the update rechecks the authority before
it signs. This read changes neither the stored token nor its deployment wallet.

## Prerequisites

- A deployed token with the status `active`
- The `tokens:admin` permission on the API key

## How it works

<HowItWorks>

<Step number={1} title="View the current settings">

Review the authorities and the configuration of the token before you change anything.

<StepPanel>
<Tabs items={["UI", "API"]} groupId="how-it-works">
<Tab value="UI">

Open the token detail page. The **Overview** tab shows the token address, the mint authority, the
current supply, and the core metadata.

![Overview tab showing the token address, mint authority, supply, template, and decimals](/images/tokens/token-settings-overview.png)

The **Permissions** tab lists every authority and the wallet that holds it.

![Permissions tab listing the mint, freeze, metadata, and permanent delegate authorities with their current wallets](/images/tokens/token-settings-permissions.png)

The **Extensions** section shows the template and each operational flag. The flags include the
Token Access Control status, mintable, freezable, and the default account state.

![Extensions section showing the template, allowlist, mintable, freezable, and default account state values](/images/tokens/token-settings-extensions.png)

</Tab>
<Tab value="API">

Fetch the current state of the token:

```bash title="Terminal"
curl https://api.solana.com/v1/issuance/tokens/tok_abc123 \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer sk_test_..."
```

```typescript title="get-token-settings.ts"
const { data } = await res.json();
// data.token.authorities — { mintAuthority, freezeAuthority, permanentDelegate }
// data.token.extensions  — active extensions on the token
// data.token.status      — "active" | "paused"
```

</Tab>
</Tabs>
</StepPanel>

</Step>

<Step number={2} title="Rotate an authority">

Move a token authority to a different wallet. Rotate an authority to move signing responsibility,
or to hand control to an external key holder.

<StepPanel>
<Tabs items={["UI", "API"]} groupId="how-it-works">
<Tab value="UI">

1. Open the **Permissions** tab of the token detail page.
2. Select **Edit** next to the authority you want to change.
3. Select another controlled wallet, or select **Use custom address** and enter one.
4. Select **Save authority**.

![Authority dialog showing the current authority wallet, the list of controlled wallets, and the Save authority control](/images/tokens/token-authority-edit.png)

> After you rotate an authority to an external wallet, SDP can no longer sign the operations that
> need it. Rotate the authority back to a controlled wallet to use the SDP deploy, mint, and
> compliance actions again.

</Tab>
<Tab value="API">

SDP signs the authority rotation:

```bash title="Terminal"
curl -X POST https://api.solana.com/v1/issuance/tokens/tok_abc123/authority \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer sk_test_..." \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -H "Idempotency-Key: rotate-001" \
  -d '{
    "authority": {
      "type": "mintAuthority",
      "newAuthority": "9aBCd...4eEf"
    }
  }'
```

`type` accepts `mintAuthority`, `freezeAuthority`, or `permanentDelegate`.

</Tab>
</Tabs>
</StepPanel>

</Step>

<Step number={3} title="Clear an authority">

Clearing an authority removes it from the token permanently. You cannot undo it. The token then
stops being mintable, freezable, or delegatable, depending on which authority you clear.

<StepPanel>
<Tabs items={["UI", "API"]} groupId="how-it-works">
<Tab value="UI">

1. Open the **Permissions** tab of the token detail page.
2. Select **Edit** next to the authority you want to clear.
3. Set the new authority to **None**.
4. Select **Save authority**.
5. Read the confirmation dialog. It explains what the change costs you, for example
   "Set Mint Authority to None?".
6. Select **Yes, set to None**.

</Tab>
<Tab value="API">

Set `newAuthority` to `null` to clear the authority:

```typescript title="revoke-authority.ts"
body: JSON.stringify({
  authority: {
    type: "mintAuthority",
    newAuthority: null,
  },
}),
```

After you clear the mint authority, nobody can ever mint this token again. The change is permanent
and you cannot undo it.

</Tab>
</Tabs>
</StepPanel>

</Step>

</HowItWorks>

## Wallet operations

### Overview
Source: https://platform.solana.com/docs/wallet-operations

> Configure the controls, permissions, and balances of a custody wallet.

This section covers the controls that SDP applies to a custody wallet, and the record it keeps of
every decision.

A **wallet policy** applies to every operation on the wallet. The same policy covers payments,
ramps, issuance, signing, and calls to onchain programs. The part of SDP that starts the operation
does not change the result.

## What's in this section

- [Wallet policies](/docs/wallet-operations/policies). Set the default decision, restrict
  destinations, cap amounts, allow or deny operations, require an approval, and read the audit
  record.
- [Wallet balances](/docs/wallet-operations/balances). Read the token balances of a custody wallet,
  with a USD value when a price source is configured.

## Which wallet identifier to use

SDP gives every wallet two identifiers. Use the right one, or the request returns `404`.

| Identifier | Where it comes from | Where you use it |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Provider wallet ID, for example `privy_wallet_123` | The `walletId` field of `GET /v1/wallets` | The `{walletId}` path segment of every endpoint on this page, and the body of `POST /v1/wallets/default-wallet` |
| SDP wallet ID, for example `cwlt_abc123` | The `id` field of `GET /v1/wallets` | The `sourceCustodyWalletId` and `destinationCustodyWalletId` fields of the payments and ramps endpoints |

The endpoints on this page accept the provider wallet ID only. They do not accept the SDP wallet ID
and they do not accept the wallet address.

## Where these endpoints live

The wallet policy and balance endpoints sit under `/v1/payments/wallets`. They apply to the whole
wallet, not only to payments. A policy can cover the transfer, payment, ramp, issuance, and program
operation families.

## Related

- [Set up wallets](/docs/guides/setup-wallets). Create the wallet before you configure its
  controls.
- [Payments](/docs/payments). The payment and ramp flows that use a wallet with a policy.
- [Manage API keys](/docs/developing-with-sdp/manage-api-keys). An API key policy can narrow a
  wallet policy, or send an operation for approval. It can never widen what the wallet policy
  allows.

---

### Wallet policies
Source: https://platform.solana.com/docs/wallet-operations/policies

> Set the controls on a custody wallet, and read the record of every policy decision.

A **wallet policy** limits how a custody wallet moves funds, and which supported operations it can
run. SDP starts from default allow. It then applies the active wallet control profile, and any
policy field you configure. SDP enforces the policy before each wallet operation runs.

Read and write a policy with `GET` and `PUT` on `/v1/payments/wallets/{walletId}/policies`. The
`{walletId}` path segment takes the provider wallet ID, for example `privy_wallet_123`. It does not
accept the SDP wallet ID, and it does not accept the wallet address. See
[Which wallet identifier to use](/docs/wallet-operations#which-wallet-identifier-to-use).

Use a policy on a treasury wallet, on an automated payout wallet, and on any custody wallet where
an unbounded outbound flow would be a liability.

## Reading a wallet's policies

<Tabs items={["curl", "TypeScript"]}>
<Tab value="curl">
```bash title="Terminal"
curl https://api.solana.com/v1/payments/wallets/privy_wallet_123/policies \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer sk_test_..."
```
</Tab>
<Tab value="TypeScript">
```typescript title="get-wallet-policies.ts"
const response = await fetch(
  "https://api.solana.com/v1/payments/wallets/privy_wallet_123/policies",
  { headers: { Authorization: "Bearer sk_test_..." } }
);
const { data } = await response.json();
// data.policy.destinationAllowlist: string[]
// data.policy.maxTransferAmount?: string
// data.policy.maxDailyAmount?: string
// data.policy.controlProfile?.providerMappingStatus
// data.policy.audit?.recentEvaluations
```
</Tab>
</Tabs>

SDP wraps the payload in the standard `data` and `meta` envelope. The policy sits under a `policy`
key:

```json title="response.json"
{
  "data": {
    "policy": {
      "walletId": "privy_wallet_123",
      "destinationAllowlist": ["7xKXz...9fGh", "5aBCd...2eFg"],
      "maxTransferAmount": "100.00",
      "maxDailyAmount": "1000.00",
      "defaultAction": "allow",
      "controlProfile": {
        "id": "wcp_abc123",
        "status": "active",
        "activeRevisionId": "wcpr_abc123",
        "revisionId": "wcpr_abc123",
        "revisionNumber": 3,
        "defaultAction": "allow",
        "rules": [
          {
            "id": "approval-required",
            "kind": "approval",
            "families": ["payment", "ramp"],
            "action": "approval_required",
            "name": "Approval checks"
          }
        ],
        "providerMappingStatus": "not_applicable",
        "createdAt": "2026-05-14T08:00:00Z",
        "updatedAt": "2026-05-14T10:15:00Z",
        "activatedAt": "2026-05-14T10:15:00Z"
      },
      "audit": {
        "recentEvaluations": [
          {
            "walletOperationId": "wop_abc123",
            "policyEvaluationId": "peval_abc123",
            "operationFamily": "payment",
            "operationType": "payment_transfer_execute",
            "asset": "USDC",
            "amount": "100.00",
            "destination": "7xKXz...9fGh",
            "status": "pending_approval",
            "decision": "approval_required",
            "reasonCode": "wallet_policy_match",
            "reason": "Payment matched approval policy.",
            "requiresApproval": true,
            "approvalRequestId": "appr_abc123",
            "operationCreatedAt": "2026-05-14T10:20:00Z",
            "operationUpdatedAt": "2026-05-14T10:20:00Z",
            "evaluatedAt": "2026-05-14T10:20:00Z"
          }
        ]
      },
      "createdAt": "2026-05-14T08:00:00Z",
      "updatedAt": "2026-05-14T10:15:00Z"
    }
  },
  "meta": { "requestId": "req_...", "timestamp": "2026-05-18T00:00:00.000Z" }
}
```

Every amount field is a decimal string in display units. `"100.00"` means 100 tokens, whatever the
mint's decimal count is. This is the same convention as a transfer request. See
[Transfer limits](#transfer-limits) for how SDP enforces `maxTransferAmount` and `maxDailyAmount`.

## Default allow and active controls

Wallet policy evaluation starts from default allow. When the wallet has no control profile, a
supported wallet operation runs unless another product check rejects it.

When you activate a control profile, SDP evaluates its rules first. SDP then returns a `decision`
with one of six values: `allow`, `deny`, `approval_required`, `provider_approval_required`,
`review`, or `not_evaluated`.

- `provider_approval_required` means the operation waits for an approval in the custody provider's
  own policy system. SDP holds the operation, as it does for `approval_required`.
- `not_evaluated` means SDP holds no policy decision for the operation. SDP rejects the operation.

The `controlProfile` object shows the active revision, which SDP never changes in place. Treat
`revisionId` and `revisionNumber` as audit references. A policy evaluation records which revision
was active when SDP checked the wallet operation.

### Dashboard actions

The authoring flow in the dashboard offers three actions: **Allow**, **Deny**, and **Require
approval**.

Choose **Require approval** when an operator must decide whether an operation can continue. SDP
then holds the operation and creates an approval request.

`review` is still a possible result of an API evaluation. It comes from a legacy path or a safety
path, such as an unrecognized policy rule. It appears in audit records. It is not an authoring
option in the dashboard, and it is not a separate human-review workflow. Do not use it to model
operator approval. Use `approval_required` instead.

## Rule kinds

A control profile revision holds an ordered list of rules. Each rule either matches the operation
or does not match it. SDP takes the decisions of the rules that match and applies the strictest
one. When no rule matches, SDP applies the revision's `defaultAction`. For every kind except
`velocity`, `action` is the decision that a match produces.

| Kind | Matches | Fields |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `operation_family` | Operations in the named families. | `family`, `families` |
| `operation_type` | Operations of the named types. | `operationType`, `operationTypes` |
| `asset` | Operations moving one of the named mints. | `asset`, `assets` |
| `destination` | Destinations on the allowlist, or off the blocklist. | `allowlist`, `blocklist`, `destination`, `destinations` |
| `amount` | A single operation's amount inside `[min, max]` for the named mints. Outside the bounds the rule denies. | `min`, `max`, `asset`, `assets` |
| `velocity` | The rolling sum of prior operations plus this one exceeds `max` for the named mints. | `scope`, `window`, `max`, `asset`, `assets`, `operationTypes` |
| `approval` | Selectors match; holds the operation for an approval group. | `families`, `operationTypes`, `assets`, `approvalGroupId` |
| `always` | Every operation. | none |

### Velocity limits

A `velocity` rule caps volume over a rolling window, instead of capping one operation:

```json title="velocity-rule.json"
{
  "id": "daily-usdc-transfers",
  "kind": "velocity",
  "scope": "organization",
  "window": "P1D",
  "max": "100000",
  "asset": "EPjFWdd5AufqSSqeM2qN1xzybapC8G4wEGGkZwyTDt1v",
  "operationTypes": ["payment_transfer_execute"],
  "action": "approval_required"
}
```

- `scope` chooses whose history counts: `wallet` (the default), `organization`, or `api_key`.
- `window` is an ISO 8601 duration in days, hours, and minutes, such as `PT1H`, `P1D`, or
  `P1DT12H`. SDP rejects weeks, months, years, and seconds.
- `max` is a decimal string in the display units of the asset. As with the `amount` kind, the rule
  must name at least one mint.
- The window sums every wallet operation for that scope and mint that SDP has decided, that has not
  failed, and that nobody canceled. `operationTypes` narrows that sum. An operation that still
  waits for its own policy decision does not count, so two concurrent requests never block each
  other.
- `action` is the decision that SDP applies when the operation passes the limit. The default is
  `deny`. Below the limit the rule produces no decision at all. It does not allow the operation, so
  it never overrides a stricter rule beside it. Set `action: "approval_required"` to send an
  outlier into the approval flow instead of refusing it.
- A request with `Dry-Run: true` reports the velocity verdict against the current history, and
  records nothing.

## Operation permissions

A wallet policy can match an operation at two levels:

- An **operation family** rule applies to every evaluated operation in a broad product area.
- An **operation type** rule matches one exact operation identifier. It takes precedence when you
  need a narrower decision.

These are wallet policy selectors, not API key permissions. An API key permission such as
`payments:write` or `tokens:write` decides whether a caller can call an endpoint. An operation
permission decides what the selected wallet can do after SDP authorizes the request.

The wallet policy is the baseline. An API key policy can narrow what a key can do, or send an
operation for approval. It can never widen what the wallet policy allows. See
[Manage API keys](/docs/developing-with-sdp/manage-api-keys) for caller permissions.

### Operation families

| Family | Description | Current evaluated operations |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `payment` | Outbound single and batch payments. | Single and batch transfer execution |
| `ramp` | Fiat-to-crypto and crypto-to-fiat ramp activity. | Onramp and offramp quote creation |
| `issuance` | Token lifecycle actions signed by the wallet. | Mint, burn, seize, and authority-update execution |
| `program` | Onchain program interactions signed by the wallet. | No current public operation type |
| `transfer` | Generic direct-transfer family reserved for operations outside the payment workflow. | No current public operation type |

A family with no current public operation type is still a valid policy value. It does not match a
public SDP flow until SDP emits an operation in that family.

### Exact operation types

| Operation type | Family | What it controls |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `payment_transfer_execute` | `payment` | Executes one outbound payment transfer from the wallet. |
| `payment_transfer_batch_execute` | `payment` | Executes an outbound batch and evaluates the aggregate amount before submission. |
| `ramp_onramp_quote` | `ramp` | Creates an onramp quote that delivers crypto to the destination wallet. |
| `ramp_offramp_quote` | `ramp` | Creates an offramp quote that draws crypto from the source wallet. |
| `issuance_mint_execute` | `issuance` | Executes a token mint using the configured signing wallet. |
| `issuance_burn_execute` | `issuance` | Executes a token burn using the configured signing wallet. |
| `issuance_force_burn_execute` | `issuance` | Force-burns tokens from a holder account. |
| `issuance_seize_execute` | `issuance` | Seizes tokens into the issuer-controlled destination. |
| `issuance_update_authority_execute` | `issuance` | Changes a token authority using the current authority wallet. |
| `issuance_freeze_execute` | `issuance` | Freezes a holder token account using the freeze authority wallet. |
| `issuance_unfreeze_execute` | `issuance` | Thaws a frozen holder token account using the freeze authority wallet. |
| `issuance_pause_execute` | `issuance` | Pauses all token transfers using the pause authority wallet. |
| `issuance_unpause_execute` | `issuance` | Resumes token transfers using the pause authority wallet. |
| `issuance_metadata_update_execute` | `issuance` | Rewrites onchain token metadata using the metadata authority wallet. |
| `recurring_payment_create` | `payment` | Creates a recurring payment schedule. |
| `recurring_payment_update` | `payment` | Updates a recurring payment schedule. |
| `recurring_payment_collection` | `payment` | Collects a due recurring payment. |

Operation-type matching is exact, and it is case-sensitive. The API accepts only the identifiers
above, so you cannot activate a rule for an operation that SDP never emits.

## Policy evaluation and audit records

SDP records each supported action against the wallet as a **wallet operation**, before evaluation
runs. That record covers the attempt, whatever its outcome.

SDP records a **policy evaluation** once it decides what should happen. That record holds the
verdict, plus a snapshot of the operation and of the policy that decided it, as both stood at that
moment.

`audit.recentEvaluations` returns the most recent decisions for the wallet, so support staff and
your own operators can review:

- which operation SDP evaluated (`walletOperationId`, `operationFamily`, `operationType`)
- which decision SDP made (`decision`, `reasonCode`, `reason`, `requiresApproval`)
- whether SDP created an approval request (`approvalRequestId`)
- when SDP created, updated, and evaluated the operation

Use these records to explain an allow, deny, approval-required, or review outcome. They are an
operational summary for an audit, not the full payload from the provider.

## Provider mapping status

`providerMappingStatus` tells you whether SDP has also mapped a policy revision into the native
policy system of a custody provider or a ramp provider. SDP enforces the current payment wallet
controls itself, first.

A value of `not_applicable` means that revision has no provider-native mapping. A value of
`pending`, `partial`, or `failed` means SDP still evaluates the operation. Do not assume that the
provider holds the same rule in full.

## Destination allowlist

`destinationAllowlist` is a wallet policy control on outbound destinations. It is not the
**Token Access Control** allowlist of a token, which controls who may hold the token itself.

The value is a list of onchain destination addresses. Each one is a base-58 Solana address of 32 to
44 characters. When you set the list, `POST /v1/payments/transfers` rejects any destination that is
not in it.

- A wallet holds at most **500 addresses**.
- Each entry is one onchain address. There are no patterns, no ranges, and no address books.
- An empty allowlist (`[]`) means no restriction on destinations. To enforce the list, add at least
  one entry.

`destinationAllowlist` and the `destination` rule kind are two separate controls, and you set them
in two different places. `destinationAllowlist` is a field of the wallet policy itself. A
`destination` rule is one entry in the `rules` array of a control profile revision, and it carries
its own `allowlist` and `blocklist` fields. See [Rule kinds](#rule-kinds) for the rule form.

Use the allowlist to limit an automated wallet, such as a hot wallet that should only ever pay a
known set of counterparties. Use it for treasury control as well, such as an operating wallet that
may send only to the corporate cold-storage address.

## Transfer limits

A transfer limit always applies to one token, identified by its mint address. Native SOL uses its
well-known mint address. A limit is never one cap across several tokens.

Both limits are optional:

- **`maxTransferAmount`** caps one transfer. SDP rejects any single `POST /v1/payments/transfers`
  above this amount. SDP compares the value against the `amount` of the request.
- **`maxDailyAmount`** caps one UTC calendar day. The day window resets at 00:00 UTC. SDP adds the
  `amount` of the new request to the sum of that wallet's outbound transfers of the **same token**
  in the current day, counting the `pending`, `processing`, `confirmed`, and `finalized` states.

You configure one threshold, and SDP enforces it separately for each token. A wallet with
`maxDailyAmount: "1000"` can therefore send 1000 USDC and 1000 SOL in the same UTC day. There is no
combined cap across mints.

If you need a different threshold per token, for example 10,000 USDC per day but 50 SOL per day,
split the work across separate wallets.

Set both limits. The per-transfer cap catches an obvious mistake. The daily cap limits the total
that many small transfers can move, when someone submits them in a coordinated attack.

## Updating policies

`PUT /v1/payments/wallets/{walletId}/policies` replaces the whole policy. The request body becomes
the new policy state in full. To remove the allowlist, send `destinationAllowlist: []`. To drop a
transfer limit, leave the field out of the next PUT.

<Tabs items={["curl", "TypeScript"]}>
<Tab value="curl">
```bash title="Terminal"
curl -X PUT https://api.solana.com/v1/payments/wallets/privy_wallet_123/policies \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer sk_test_..." \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "destinationAllowlist": [
      "7xKXz...9fGh",
      "5aBCd...2eFg"
    ],
    "maxTransferAmount": "100.00",
    "maxDailyAmount": "1000.00"
  }'
```
</Tab>
<Tab value="TypeScript">
```typescript title="update-wallet-policies.ts"
await fetch(
  "https://api.solana.com/v1/payments/wallets/privy_wallet_123/policies",
  {
    method: "PUT",
    headers: {
      "Authorization": "Bearer sk_test_...",
      "Content-Type": "application/json",
    },
    body: JSON.stringify({
      destinationAllowlist: ["7xKXz...9fGh", "5aBCd...2eFg"],
      maxTransferAmount: "100.00",
      maxDailyAmount: "1000.00",
    }),
  }
);
```
</Tab>
</Tabs>

Because PUT replaces the whole policy, treat a policy edit like an ordinary form submission. Read
the current state, show it for editing, then PUT the complete updated object. Do not build a
partial patch.

## Interaction with compliance

A wallet policy enforces structural limits: where funds can go, how much can move, and how fast. It
does not replace compliance screening.

If your organization has compliance screening enabled, SDP screens the destination address as a
separate check, next to the allowlist match. Either layer can reject a transfer, and a transfer
must pass both to reach the network.

See the [Compliance API reference](/docs/reference/api/compliance) for the address-screening flows
that work alongside a policy.

## Related

- [Payouts and disbursements](/docs/payments/send-payouts). Run an outbound batch from a wallet
  that has a policy.
- [Basic payment](/docs/payments/send-basic-payment). The transfer endpoint that the policy applies
  to.
- [Wallet balances](/docs/wallet-operations/balances). Read the current balance to size a transfer
  limit.

---

### Wallet balances
Source: https://platform.solana.com/docs/wallet-operations/balances

> Read the token balances of a custody wallet, with a USD value when a price source is configured.

`GET /v1/payments/wallets/{walletId}/balances` returns the balances that a custody wallet holds. It
returns the native **SOL** balance and every **SPL token** balance.

Each entry carries the raw amount, the amount in display units, the decimal count, and a USD value
when a price source is configured.

SOL is always the first entry. SDP returns it with `token: "SOL"` and
`mint: "So11111111111111111111111111111111111111112"`.

The `{walletId}` path segment takes the provider wallet ID, for example `privy_wallet_123`. It does
not accept the SDP wallet ID, and it does not accept the wallet address. See
[Which wallet identifier to use](/docs/wallet-operations#which-wallet-identifier-to-use).

## Request

<Tabs items={["curl", "TypeScript", "Java"]}>
<Tab value="curl">
```bash title="Terminal"
curl https://api.solana.com/v1/payments/wallets/privy_wallet_123/balances \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer sk_test_..."
```
</Tab>
<Tab value="TypeScript">
```typescript title="get-wallet-balances.ts"
const response = await fetch(
  "https://api.solana.com/v1/payments/wallets/privy_wallet_123/balances",
  { headers: { Authorization: "Bearer sk_test_..." } }
);
const { data } = await response.json();
// data.walletBalances.balances: TokenBalance[]
```
</Tab>
<Tab value="Java">
```java title="GetWalletBalances.java"
HttpRequest request = HttpRequest.newBuilder()
    .uri(URI.create("https://api.solana.com/v1/payments/wallets/privy_wallet_123/balances"))
    .header("Authorization", "Bearer sk_test_...")
    .GET()
    .build();
```
</Tab>
</Tabs>

## Response shape

SDP wraps the payload in the standard `data` and `meta` envelope. The balances sit under a
`walletBalances` key:

```json title="response.json"
{
  "data": {
    "walletBalances": {
      "walletId": "privy_wallet_123",
      "address": "3xYZa...2aBc",
      "balances": [
        {
          "token": "SOL",
          "mint": "So11111111111111111111111111111111111111112",
          "amount": "2500000000",
          "uiAmount": "2.5",
          "decimals": 9
        },
        {
          "token": "USDC",
          "mint": "EPjFWdd5AufqSSqeM2qN1xzybapC8G4wEGGkZwyTDt1v",
          "amount": "1500000000",
          "uiAmount": "1500.00",
          "decimals": 6,
          "usdPrice": 1.0,
          "usdValue": 1500.0
        }
      ]
    }
  },
  "meta": { "requestId": "req_...", "timestamp": "2026-05-18T00:00:00.000Z" }
}
```

Each balance has these fields:

| Field | Notes |
| --- | --- |
| `token` | The token symbol when SDP knows it. Otherwise the onchain mint address. |
| `mint` | The onchain mint address. |
| `amount` | The amount in the smallest unit. It is a string, to keep full precision. |
| `uiAmount` | The amount in display units, as a decimal string. SDP divides `amount` by 10 to the power of `decimals`. |
| `decimals` | The decimal count of the token. |
| `usdPrice` | The USD price of one token. SDP omits it when it has no price data. |
| `usdValue` | The USD value of the whole balance. SDP multiplies `usdPrice` by `uiAmount`. SDP omits it when it has no price data. |
| `confidential` | Reserved for confidential transfer balances. It is absent for a standard balance. |

## Use cases

- **Account dashboards**. Show the contents of a custody wallet to the person who operates it.
- **Balance checks before a transfer**. Confirm that a wallet holds enough of one token before you
  start a payout batch.
- **Treasury accounting**. Take regular snapshots into your own ledger.

## Pricing freshness

When SDP returns a USD value, the price comes from the configured price source, and it is the most
recent quote that source has given.

The source and its update cadence depend on how your deployment is configured. Confirm both with
your operations team before you use `usdValue` for a balance-sheet decision. Until you have, treat
`amount` and `uiAmount` as the authoritative values, and convert them with your own price feed.

If no price source is configured, SDP omits `usdPrice` and `usdValue` instead of returning zero.
The missing field means "unknown", not "$0.00", so your code can decide how to handle the gap.

## Comparison to a Solana RPC call

You can also list SPL token balances yourself. Call `getTokenAccountsByOwner` on a Solana RPC
endpoint, then decode the token account data it returns.

Reasons to call the SDP `balances` endpoint instead:

- **Token resolution**. SDP resolves a mint address to a symbol when it knows one. A raw RPC call
  returns mint addresses only.
- **USD pricing**. An RPC endpoint has no price data.
- **No RPC dependency**. You call SDP already, so you keep one fewer external integration.

Reasons to call the RPC endpoint instead:

- **State at an exact slot**. An audit can require the wallet's balances at one specific slot.
- **Confidential transfer balances**. Full support for the extension is on the RPC side.
- **Latency**. The RPC endpoint is one hop closer to the Solana cluster.

## Related

- [Wallet policies](/docs/wallet-operations/policies). Set a transfer limit from the balances you
  read here.
- [Payouts and disbursements](/docs/payments/send-payouts). Check the balance before you run a
  batch.
- [Set up wallets](/docs/guides/setup-wallets). Create the wallets whose balances this endpoint
  reports.

## Payments

### Overview
Source: https://platform.solana.com/docs/payments

> Build payments on Solana with SDP, from a single transfer to fiat onramps and offramps.

SDP gives you a Solana-native payments stack. It covers stablecoin transfers, fiat onramps and
offramps, and the records you need to reconcile them.

This section follows the structure of the
[public Solana payments documentation](https://solana.com/docs/payments). Each workflow below names
the SDP APIs you call to build it.

Create a custody wallet and a token before you start. See
[Set up wallets](/docs/guides/setup-wallets) and
[Tokenize an asset](/docs/tokens/tokenize-an-asset).

## What is in this section

- **[How payments work on SDP](/docs/payments/concepts)**. Wallets, tokens, signing modes, fees,
  and the transfer data model.
- **Send payments.** The outbound flows.
  - [Basic payment](/docs/payments/send-basic-payment). One transfer, in either signing mode.
  - [Payment with memo](/docs/payments/send-payment-with-memo). Attach an order reference or a
    customer reference to a transfer.
  - [Payouts and disbursements](/docs/payments/send-payouts). Batched outbound transfers, and how
    to reconcile them.
- **Accept payments.** The inbound flows.
  - [Accept payments](/docs/payments/accept-overview). The receiving-address convention and the
    integration options.
  - [Verifying a payment](/docs/payments/accept-verification). What each transfer status means, and
    what finality means.
  - [Indexing and reconciliation](/docs/payments/accept-indexing). List inbound transfers for your
    own ledger.
- **Ramps.** Fiat onramps and offramps.
  - [Ramps](/docs/payments/ramps). Corridor discovery, rate estimates, and the shape of a Ramp
    Quote request.
  - [Ramp providers](/docs/payments/ramps-providers). The capability matrix and the configuration
    for all seven ramp providers.

[Wallet operations](/docs/wallet-operations) documents wallet-wide controls and balances.

## The underlying API

Every page in this section links to endpoints in the generated
[Payments API reference](/docs/reference/api/payments). The Payments API area sits under
`/v1/payments`. It groups into four parts: `transfers`, `ramps`, `wallets/.../balances`, and
`wallets/.../policies`.
