### Token templates
Source: https://platform.solana.com/docs/reference/issuance-token-types

> Choose a token template, and see the default controls that each one applies.

A **token template** is a fixed composition of Token-2022 extensions for one class of asset. In the
dashboard, the control is labeled **Template**.

`GET /v1/issuance/templates` returns the templates your deployment offers.
`GET /v1/issuance/templates/{templateId}` returns the current definition of one template. Treat the
API as the source of truth for the list and the defaults.

<Callout type="warn">
This page gives general guidance. It is not legal advice. Regulatory treatment depends on the
jurisdiction, and on how the instrument is structured. Confirm your classification before you
deploy a token.
</Callout>

The three templates below cover the common institutional cases:

| Template | Defaults | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `stablecoin` | 6 decimals, permanent delegate + pausable extensions, default account state initialized | Intended for fiat-backed token patterns with compliance controls. |
| `tokenized-security` | 8 decimals, allowlist on by default and changeable, permanent delegate + pausable + scaled UI amount extensions, default account state frozen | Regulated asset flows with stronger defaults. |
| `custom` | 9 decimals default (up to 18 max), extension set is fully configurable | Use when your requirements do not match the stablecoin or tokenized-security templates. |

Each template also sets the token's **Token Access Control** mode. The mode is `allowlist`,
`blocklist`, or `disabled`. SDP enforces it onchain, over who can hold or receive the token.

Token Access Control is distinct from a wallet's own destination allowlist. The destination
allowlist is a wallet-policy concern.

## Selecting a template

Each template is a vetted, fixed set of Token-2022 extensions for a specific class of asset. It is
not a menu of individual options. Choose the template by the nature of the instrument you issue.
The `custom` template covers an asset that fits neither the stablecoin nor the tokenized-security
model.

### Stablecoin

Use this template for a token that is pegged to a fiat currency and redeemable at par (1:1). It
applies the compliance controls that are typical of a regulated fiat token:

- The **pausable** extension lets you pause transfers for every holder of the token at once. Use it
  in an emergency. This is different from a freeze, which stops one holder's balance.
- The **permanent delegate** lets you seize or claw back tokens in response to a compliance event.

A stablecoin cannot pay interest or yield to its holders. This reflects the payment-stablecoin
frameworks, such as the U.S. GENIUS Act and the EU's MiCA, which prohibit an issuer from paying
interest on the token itself. Issue an interest-bearing or yield-bearing product as a tokenized
security, which is usually a fund, rather than as a stablecoin.

### Tokenized security

Use this template for a regulated instrument, such as equity, debt, or fund shares. It applies the
stablecoin controls together with stronger defaults:

- An **allowlist** is on by default, and you can change that setting.
- New accounts are **frozen by default**, so a holder must be approved before they can transact.
- The **scaled UI amount** extension supports a corporate action, such as a split or a share-class
  rebasing.

An interest-bearing or yield-bearing instrument, such as a debt token or a fund token, also falls
under this template.

### Custom

This template corresponds to the **Non-Security Digital Asset** classification in the issuance
pages. Those assets are neither fiat stablecoins nor regulated securities. Commodities, real
estate, and collectibles are examples.

The template offers the full Token-2022 extension set, including transfer fees, transfer hooks,
non-transferable behavior, and interest. Use it when the stablecoin and tokenized-security
templates do not match the instrument.

### Summary

| Instrument | Template |
| --- | --- |
| Pegged to a fiat currency, redeemable 1:1, with no yield | `stablecoin` |
| Regulated security (equity, debt, or fund), or an instrument that pays a return | `tokenized-security` |
| Any other asset, or one requiring extensions the other templates do not offer | `custom` (Non-Security Digital Asset) |

<Callout type="warn">
SDP sets the Token-2022 extensions when it creates the mint, and nobody can change them afterward.
The template you select is therefore permanent for that token. To change it, issue a new token.
</Callout>

## Amount format

The mint, burn, seize, and force-burn request bodies take `amount` as a **decimal string in UI
units**. That is the human-readable token value, for example `"1"` or `"1.5"`.

SDP converts the value to onchain base units, using the token's `decimals`. Wallet balance
responses differ: they return both a raw `amount` and a `uiAmount`.

---

### Infrastructure provider onboarding
Source: https://platform.solana.com/docs/reference/provider-onboarding

> How a vendor contributes a new infrastructure provider integration to the SDP codebase.

This page is for a vendor who wants to contribute an infrastructure provider integration to SDP. It
covers the intake forms, the evaluation criteria, and what the contributed pull request must
contain.

This page is not an activation guide. It does not explain how to enable an existing provider for
your organization, and it does not explain how to configure a provider on a self-hosted deployment.
If you arrived here looking for either of those, see
[Ramp providers](/docs/payments/ramps-providers) for how SDP checks provider availability on every
call, and see the
[self-hosting environment reference](/docs/self-hosting/env-reference) for the variables a
self-hosted deployment reads.

SDP supports infrastructure provider integrations across custody, RPC, compliance, and ramps. SDP
adds more integration categories as the product expands.

An onboarded provider appears as an available integration. SDP does not endorse or recommend it.
Each institution that uses SDP is responsible for its own provider due diligence.

## Categories and intake forms

Select the category that matches your integration. Complete the intake form, and review the
criteria, before you open a pull request.

| Category | Intake form | Criteria |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Custodial enterprise wallet | [Complete custody intake](https://solanafoundation.typeform.com/to/wShiq9SN) | [Download custody criteria PDF](/provider-onboarding/custodial-wallet-vendor.pdf) |
| RPC infrastructure | [Complete RPC intake](https://solanafoundation.typeform.com/to/cq5m65jI) | [Download RPC criteria PDF](/provider-onboarding/rpc-providers.pdf) |
| Ramp | [Complete ramp intake](https://solanafoundation.typeform.com/to/sxTGbwXt) | [Download ramp criteria PDF](/provider-onboarding/ramp-criteria.pdf) |

Contact the SDP team before you open a pull request if your integration is for compliance, or for
another infrastructure category without a published intake.

## Onboarding steps

1. Review the criteria PDF for your category.
2. Complete the matching intake form.
3. Provide sandbox or playground API access.
4. Share your documentation, test credentials, supported Solana clusters, rate limits, and sandbox
   limitations.
5. Build the SDP integration, with tests and documentation.
6. Open a pull request that links to the intake submission or to the tracking issue.

The SDP team reviews intake completeness within five business days. Gate evaluation usually takes
one to three weeks. The exact time depends on the category, the completeness of the documentation,
and the technical validation the category requires.

## Evaluation

Each category uses the finalized criteria linked above. Every review starts with the hard gates. A
scored evaluation follows, where one applies.

SDP evaluates the following:

- Solana compatibility for the category.
- Stable sandbox or playground access.
- Clear API and integration documentation.
- Predictable error handling and testability.
- Operational readiness and support.
- The regulatory, compliance, or security posture that the category requires.

The SDP team can track a provider that does not clear the required gates, for future support. SDP
does not present that provider as available until the gaps are resolved.

A provider that clears evaluation becomes available according to the deployment's configuration.
It is either generally available to every organization, or it is gated behind a per-organization
Manual Provider Activation. The gated path applies when commercial or operational onboarding is
still required.

## Access requirements

Provide access that supports repeatable validation, including:

- Sandbox API keys, or equivalent credentials.
- Test accounts, wallets, endpoints, or settlement routes, where the flow requires them.
- The Solana clusters you support.
- Known rate limits, feature conditions, and sandbox limitations.
- A technical support contact for the review.

## Pull request expectations

An SDP infrastructure provider contribution usually includes:

- Provider metadata and capability registration.
- API support for setup, configuration, and the runtime operations of the category.
- Dashboard support, where it applies.
- Tests for setup, success paths, failure states, disabled configuration, and missing credentials.
- User-facing documentation for setup, sandbox behavior, and provider limits.

Open the pull request after your intake is complete. You can also open it after the SDP team
creates a tracking issue while the intake is being finalized.

---

### Documentation for AI
Source: https://platform.solana.com/docs/reference/docs-for-ai

> The machine-readable entry points that agents and AI systems use to read SDP docs and APIs.

Use this page when you need the public AI-facing entry points for the Solana Developer Platform.

## Machine-readable resources

- [llms.txt](/docs/ai/llms.txt) is a concise discovery file. It lists the canonical URLs, the
  supported API areas, and the key starting pages.
- [llms-full.txt](/docs/ai/llms-full.txt) is an expanded docs map. SDP generates it from the docs
  navigation and the public API reference.
- [OpenAPI](/docs/reference/api) is the human-readable API reference. SDP generates it from the
  public contract.
- [OpenAPI JSON](https://api.solana.com/openapi.json) is the machine-readable API contract for the
  public SDP API.
- [API llms.txt](https://api.solana.com/llms.txt) is the API-only discovery entry point. It covers
  the endpoint families and the authentication expectations.
- [Postman collection](/docs/reference/postman-collection) is a downloadable public collection. SDP
  generates it from the same OpenAPI source.

## Recommended ingestion order

1. Start with [llms.txt](/docs/ai/llms.txt).
2. Expand to [llms-full.txt](/docs/ai/llms-full.txt) when you need broader site coverage.
3. Use the [API reference](/docs/reference/api) and the
   [OpenAPI JSON](https://api.solana.com/openapi.json) for exact request and response schemas.
4. Use the product guides for workflow sequencing, operational constraints, and supported patterns.

## Scope

- These AI resources cover the supported public SDP API areas only.
- SDP excludes the hidden and internal-only route families on purpose.
- Treat the public docs as the source of truth, ahead of any internal implementation detail.

## Coverage focus

- Wallets and custody
- API key management
- Projects
- Token issuance and lifecycle operations
- Payments, transfers, and ramps
- Compliance screening

### Postman collection
Source: https://platform.solana.com/docs/reference/postman-collection

> Download the public SDP API Postman collection, generated from the OpenAPI contract.

SDP generates the Postman collection from the same public OpenAPI contract that produces the
[API reference](/docs/reference/api). The collection includes every end-user-facing family that the
reference publishes.

SDP excludes the internal-only endpoint families on purpose. Those families are `rpc`, `admin`,
`onboarding`, `auth`, `organizations`, and `members`.

<div>
  <a href="/docs/postman/collection.json" download>Download Postman collection</a>
  {" · "}
  <a href="/docs/postman/collection.json">Open raw JSON</a>
</div>

After you import the collection into Postman, set two variables:

- Set `baseUrl` to the SDP API environment you want to target.
- Set `sdpApiKey` to your bearer API key.

### API Keys

> API key management endpoints.

| Method | Endpoint | Summary |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `GET` | `/v1/api-keys` | List API keys |
| `POST` | `/v1/api-keys` | Create API key |
| `DELETE` | `/v1/api-keys/{keyId}` | Deactivate API key |
| `GET` | `/v1/api-keys/{keyId}` | Get API key |
| `PATCH` | `/v1/api-keys/{keyId}` | Update API key |
| `PUT` | `/v1/api-keys/{keyId}/policy-bindings` | Replace or clear API-key policy bindings |
| `POST` | `/v1/api-keys/{keyId}/policy-profiles` | Create API-key policy profile |
| `POST` | `/v1/api-keys/{keyId}/policy-profiles/{profileId}/revisions` | Create API-key policy revision |

### Projects
Source: https://platform.solana.com/docs/reference/api/projects

> Project and project member management.

| Method | Endpoint | Summary |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `GET` | `/v1/projects` | List projects |
| `GET` | `/v1/projects/{projectId}` | Get project |
| `PATCH` | `/v1/projects/{projectId}` | Update project |
| `GET` | `/v1/projects/{projectId}/api-keys` | List project API keys |
| `POST` | `/v1/projects/{projectId}/api-keys` | Create project API key |
| `GET` | `/v1/projects/{projectId}/members` | List project members |
| `POST` | `/v1/projects/{projectId}/members` | Add project member |
| `DELETE` | `/v1/projects/{projectId}/members/{memberId}` | Remove project member |
| `PATCH` | `/v1/projects/{projectId}/members/{memberId}` | Update project member |

### Issuance
Source: https://platform.solana.com/docs/reference/api/issuance

> Token issuance, allowlists, and lifecycle operations.

| Method | Endpoint | Summary |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `GET` | `/v1/issuance/templates` | List token templates |
| `GET` | `/v1/issuance/templates/{templateId}` | Get token template |
| `GET` | `/v1/issuance/tokens` | List tokens |
| `POST` | `/v1/issuance/tokens` | Create token |
| `GET` | `/v1/issuance/tokens/{tokenId}` | Get token |
| `PATCH` | `/v1/issuance/tokens/{tokenId}` | Update token |
| `GET` | `/v1/issuance/tokens/{tokenId}/allowlist` | List token allowlist |
| `POST` | `/v1/issuance/tokens/{tokenId}/allowlist` | Add token allowlist entry |
| `DELETE` | `/v1/issuance/tokens/{tokenId}/allowlist/{entryId}` | Remove token allowlist entry |
| `GET` | `/v1/issuance/tokens/{tokenId}/allowlist/labels` | List token allowlist labels |
| `GET` | `/v1/issuance/tokens/{tokenId}/audit` | Get asset audit history |
| `POST` | `/v1/issuance/tokens/{tokenId}/authority` | Execute authority update |
| `POST` | `/v1/issuance/tokens/{tokenId}/authority/prepare` | Prepare authority update |
| `POST` | `/v1/issuance/tokens/{tokenId}/burn` | Execute burn |
| `POST` | `/v1/issuance/tokens/{tokenId}/burn/prepare` | Prepare burn transaction |
| `POST` | `/v1/issuance/tokens/{tokenId}/deploy` | Deploy token |
| `POST` | `/v1/issuance/tokens/{tokenId}/deploy/confirm` | Confirm non-custodial deploy |
| `POST` | `/v1/issuance/tokens/{tokenId}/deploy/prepare` | Prepare token deploy transaction |
| `POST` | `/v1/issuance/tokens/{tokenId}/deploy/prepare-metadata` | Prepare metadata-URI follow-up transaction |
| `POST` | `/v1/issuance/tokens/{tokenId}/force-burn` | Execute force burn |
| `POST` | `/v1/issuance/tokens/{tokenId}/force-burn/prepare` | Prepare force burn transaction |
| `POST` | `/v1/issuance/tokens/{tokenId}/freeze` | Freeze account |
| `GET` | `/v1/issuance/tokens/{tokenId}/frozen` | List frozen accounts |
| `GET` | `/v1/issuance/tokens/{tokenId}/holders` | List verified holders |
| `POST` | `/v1/issuance/tokens/{tokenId}/holders` | Enroll a verified holder |
| `GET` | `/v1/issuance/tokens/{tokenId}/metadata.json` | Get public token metadata JSON |
| `POST` | `/v1/issuance/tokens/{tokenId}/mint` | Execute mint |
| `POST` | `/v1/issuance/tokens/{tokenId}/mint/prepare` | Prepare mint transaction |
| `POST` | `/v1/issuance/tokens/{tokenId}/pause` | Pause token transfers |
| `POST` | `/v1/issuance/tokens/{tokenId}/seize` | Execute seize |
| `POST` | `/v1/issuance/tokens/{tokenId}/seize/prepare` | Prepare seize transaction |
| `POST` | `/v1/issuance/tokens/{tokenId}/supply/refresh` | Refresh cached token supply |
| `GET` | `/v1/issuance/tokens/{tokenId}/transactions` | List token transactions |
| `POST` | `/v1/issuance/tokens/{tokenId}/unfreeze` | Unfreeze account |
| `POST` | `/v1/issuance/tokens/{tokenId}/unpause` | Unpause token transfers |
| `GET` | `/v1/issuance/tokens/facets` | List token filter facets |
| `GET` | `/v1/issuance/transactions` | List issuance transactions |

### Payments
Source: https://platform.solana.com/docs/reference/api/payments

> Wallet balances, transfer execution, policies, and ramps.

| Method | Endpoint | Summary |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `GET` | `/v1/payments/ramps/offramp/currency` | List off-ramp currency support |
| `GET` | `/v1/payments/ramps/onramp/currency` | List on-ramp currency support |
| `POST` | `/v1/payments/ramps/onramp/quote` | Create on-ramp quote |
| `POST` | `/v1/payments/ramps/sandbox/simulate` | Simulate sandbox transfer |
| `GET` | `/v1/payments/recurring-payments` | List recurring payments |
| `POST` | `/v1/payments/recurring-payments` | Create recurring payment |
| `GET` | `/v1/payments/recurring-payments/{id}` | Get recurring payment |
| `PATCH` | `/v1/payments/recurring-payments/{id}` | Update recurring payment |
| `POST` | `/v1/payments/recurring-payments/{id}/activate` | Activate recurring payment |
| `POST` | `/v1/payments/recurring-payments/{id}/cancel` | Cancel recurring payment |
| `POST` | `/v1/payments/recurring-payments/{id}/collect` | Collect recurring payment |
| `POST` | `/v1/payments/recurring-payments/{id}/resume` | Resume recurring payment |
| `GET` | `/v1/payments/subscription-plans` | List subscription plans |
| `POST` | `/v1/payments/subscription-plans` | Create subscription plan |
| `GET` | `/v1/payments/subscription-plans/{planId}` | Get subscription plan |
| `PATCH` | `/v1/payments/subscription-plans/{planId}` | Update subscription plan |
| `POST` | `/v1/payments/subscription-plans/{planId}/prepare-create` | Prepare subscription plan creation |
| `GET` | `/v1/payments/subscriptions` | List subscriptions |
| `POST` | `/v1/payments/subscriptions` | Create subscription |
| `GET` | `/v1/payments/subscriptions/{subscriptionId}` | Get subscription |
| `GET` | `/v1/payments/subscriptions/{subscriptionId}/collection-attempts` | List subscription collection attempts |
| `POST` | `/v1/payments/subscriptions/{subscriptionId}/prepare-authorization` | Prepare subscription authorization |
| `POST` | `/v1/payments/subscriptions/{subscriptionId}/prepare-cancel` | Prepare subscription cancellation |
| `POST` | `/v1/payments/subscriptions/{subscriptionId}/prepare-collection` | Prepare subscription collection |
| `POST` | `/v1/payments/subscriptions/{subscriptionId}/prepare-resume` | Prepare subscription resume |
| `GET` | `/v1/payments/transfer-batches` | List transfer batches |
| `POST` | `/v1/payments/transfer-batches` | Create transfer batch |
| `GET` | `/v1/payments/transfer-batches/{batchId}` | Get transfer batch |
| `POST` | `/v1/payments/transfer-batches/estimate` | Estimate transfer batch |
| `GET` | `/v1/payments/transfers` | List transfers |
| `POST` | `/v1/payments/transfers` | Execute transfer (custody) |
| `GET` | `/v1/payments/transfers/{transferId}` | Get transfer |
| `GET` | `/v1/payments/wallets/{walletId}/balances` | Get wallet balances |
| `GET` | `/v1/payments/wallets/{walletId}/policies` | Get wallet policy |
| `PUT` | `/v1/payments/wallets/{walletId}/policies` | Update wallet policy |
| `GET` | `/v1/payments/wallets/{walletId}/policies/evaluations` | List wallet policy evaluations |
| `GET` | `/v1/payments/wallets/{walletId}/policies/evaluations/{policyEvaluationId}` | Get wallet policy evaluation |
| `GET` | `/v1/payments/wallets/{walletId}/policies/revisions` | List wallet policy revisions |
| `GET` | `/v1/transactions` | List transactions |

### Asset Profiles
Source: https://platform.solana.com/docs/reference/api/asset-profiles

> Issued-asset identity and metadata profiles, plus the public token metadata URI.

| Method | Endpoint | Summary |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `GET` | `/v1/issuance/asset-profiles` | List asset profiles |
| `POST` | `/v1/issuance/asset-profiles` | Create token with asset profile |
| `DELETE` | `/v1/issuance/asset-profiles/{profileId}` | Archive asset profile |
| `GET` | `/v1/issuance/asset-profiles/{profileId}` | Get asset profile |
| `PATCH` | `/v1/issuance/asset-profiles/{profileId}` | Update asset profile |
| `GET` | `/v1/issuance/asset-profiles/by-token/{tokenId}` | Get asset profile by token |
| `GET` | `/v1/issuance/asset-profiles/field-options` | Get asset profile field options |
